findings: Circular / mutually contradictory precedence: MSA 14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, SOW 1.2 says the SOW (Schedule 1) prevails over the MSA, and Order Form 2.1–2.2 puts the Order Form above everything. No conflict can be resolved. 01_msa.md cl.14.2; 02_sow.md cl.1.2; 05_order_form.md cl.2.1–2.2

The Order Form claims top precedence but is not part of the 'Agreement' as defined: MSA 1.1 defines the Agreement as the MSA plus each Schedule and Addendum, and MSA 1.6 requires a Schedule to be expressly stated to be a Schedule. The Order Form is neither, so its precedence clause has nothing to operate on. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6; 05_order_form.md cl.2.1

Monthly Fee stated three inconsistent ways: £12,400 (MSA), £12,800 (SOW), and an Annual Contract Value of £153,600 (= £12,800 × 12) in the Order Form. 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4
Payment terms conflict three ways: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Term conflict: MSA initial term 24 months; SOW programme duration 36 months; Order Form initial term 12 months. The 36-month programme cannot be performed within either the 24-month or 12-month term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 02_sow.md cl.2.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Start date conflict: the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027) and before the Order Form was even signed (12 March 2027) — work is scheduled to begin before the contract exists. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md cl.2.2; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3, 7.3

Termination/non-renewal notice periods conflict: MSA requires 90 days' notice for convenience and renewal is governed by cl.3.3, whereas the SOW allows 30 days and the Order Form allows 30 days' non-renewal notice. 01_msa.md cl.3.2–3.3; 02_sow.md cl.2.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.2
Availability target conflict: SOW requires not less than 99.5% monthly availability while the SLA requires not less than 99.9% for the same platform. 02_sow.md cl.7.2; 04_sla.md cl.3.1
Service credit cap conflict: SOW allows credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee; SLA caps credits at 10% of the monthly Fee. 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2

Service levels commencement conflict: SOW says service levels apply only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme); Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md cl.7.1; 05_order_form.md cl.3.3
Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; SLA provides Priority 2 and 3 support only 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 04_sla.md cl.2.2; 05_order_form.md cl.3.1

'Business Day' defined twice and incompatibly: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA), in a contract governed by English law. 01_msa.md cl.1.2; 04_sla.md cl.1.1

'Security Incident' defined twice and incompatibly: DPA covers any unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction; SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of data. Many DPA incidents are not SLA incidents. 03_dpa.md cl.1.6; 04_sla.md cl.7.1

Security incident notification deadlines conflict three ways: within 24 hours (DPA), within 72 hours (SLA), within 48 hours (Information Security Policy). 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 04_sla.md cl.7.3; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1

Internal inconsistency: a Security Incident is deemed a Priority 1 Incident requiring 15-minute response and 4-hour Resolution, yet notification to Customer is allowed to take 72 hours. 04_sla.md cl.7.2–7.3

Reference to a non-existent annex: SLA points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum' for security escalation contacts; the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4; 03_dpa.md Annexes
Reference to a non-existent clause: Exit Plan refers to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3

Reference to a non-existent clause and body: Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and creates no Change Control Board, so the approval route is unworkable. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1; 01_msa.md

Reference to a non-existent section: MSA requires acceptance criteria 'set out in Schedule 1, Section 12'; the SOW (Schedule 1) has only 10 sections and contains no acceptance criteria at all. 01_msa.md cl.6.2; 02_sow.md

Acceptance mechanism conflict: MSA states no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer confirms expressly in writing; SOW deems a Deliverable accepted if Customer is silent for five Business Days. 01_msa.md cl.6.1; 02_sow.md cl.6.3

Deliverables are undefined in substance: MSA defines Deliverable as an item identified as such in a Statement of Work, but the SOW identifies none, deferring to a 'phase plan maintained by the delivery lead' — a unilateral, non-contractual document. 01_msa.md cl.1.3; 02_sow.md cl.6.1

Change control conflict: MSA requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, whereas the Change Control Procedure permits deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 01_msa.md cl.2.4; 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Escalation timetable defeats the deemed-approval clock: three escalation levels at five Business Days each (up to 15 Business Days) run past the 10 Business Day deemed-approval window, and cl.8.3 expressly prevents suspension, so a disputed change is deemed approved while still being escalated. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 8.1–8.3

Cross-reference to a rate that does not exist: Provider may charge for impact assessments 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', but the Exit Plan only sets a transition-assistance day rate and no impact assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2; 09_exit.md cl.3.2

Charge-increase conflict: MSA limits Fee increases to once per 12 months, on 60 days' notice and capped at CPI, while the Change Control Procedure states change-related charges are not subject to those notice requirements, allowing uncapped, immediate increases. 01_msa.md cl.4.4; 08_change_control.md cl.5.1, 5.3

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees and states the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum; the SOW sets a £250,000 cap; the DPA states no limitation in the Agreement applies to breaches of the Addendum or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md cl.9.2; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1

Consequential loss exclusion appears only in the SOW, which under MSA 14.2 is overridden by the MSA (which contains no such exclusion) — the exclusion is ineffective/uncertain in scope. 02_sow.md cl.9.3; 01_msa.md cl.14.2
Insurance conflict: MSA requires professional indemnity cover of not less than £5,000,000; SOW requires not less than £2,000,000 for the same engagement. 01_msa.md cl.16.1; 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Governing law conflict: MSA is governed by English law with exclusive English jurisdiction; the DPA purports to be governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md cl.15.1–15.2; 03_dpa.md cl.13.2

Internal contradiction within the DPA governing law clause: cl.13.1 adopts the Agreement's law 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and 13.2 then displaces it entirely, rendering 13.1 meaningless. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1–13.2

Audit rights contradict: MSA states that provision of the SOC 2 report leaves Customer with 'no further right to audit, inspect or attend' Provider's premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md cl.10.2; 03_dpa.md cl.9.1–9.2

Self-defeating cross-reference: MSA cl.12.2 requires Provider to make records available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but 10.2 removes all inspection rights, so the records obligation has no mechanism. 01_msa.md cl.12.2 and 10.2

Encryption conflict: DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, but the Information Security Policy requires encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data', and ordinary personal data (contact details, transaction records, loyalty identifiers) falls into the unencrypted 'Internal Data' class. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2; 06_infosec.md cl.1.2–1.3, 3.1

Confidentiality definitions conflict: MSA limits Confidential Information to material marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; under MSA 14.2 the MSA prevails, defeating the DPA protection. 01_msa.md cl.11.1, 14.2; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality survival (3 years) is shorter than the 7-year records retention obligation and the perpetual sensitivity of retained personal data, leaving retained material unprotected. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 and 12.4

Data retention/deletion obligations are mutually impossible: MSA requires all records, data and materials to be retained for 7 years after termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days after termination. 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3
Log retention conflict: security logs must be retained 18 months and then deleted, contradicting the MSA's 7-year record retention obligation. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2; 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Report/log retention 'for the duration of the Agreement' conflicts with the MSA obligation to retain records for 7 years following expiry or termination. 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3; 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Exit timetable is inconsistent with the deletion/retention windows: handover (including delivery of all Customer data) is certified only at the end of the 6-month transition period, and Annex 1 milestones run to T+90 Business Days (~4.5 months), yet data must be deleted after 90 calendar days (Exit 2.3/5.2) and within 30 days of termination (DPA 8.2). 09_exit.md cl.2.1, 2.3, 4.1, 5.2, Annex 1; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2
Data return format conflict: the Exit Plan requires return in 'the format used by Provider's systems'; the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a); 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for up to 6 months after the effective date of termination on the terms then in force, which is irreconcilable with the MSA/Order Form term ending on termination and with no fee mechanism for that period. 09_exit.md cl.2.1–2.2; 01_msa.md cl.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Transition assistance is conditioned on Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which allows Provider's exit obligations to stall and contradicts the unconditional duty in cl.1.2/3.1 that the Plan applies however the Agreement ends. 09_exit.md cl.1.2, 3.1, 3.4

Availability target and Resolution target are mathematically incompatible: 99.9% monthly availability permits only ~43 minutes of downtime, yet a Priority 1 outage may lawfully take 4 hours to resolve. 04_sla.md cl.3.1 and 5.1

Response and Resolution times are measured from Provider's own acknowledgement of the Incident in its tool, making the 15-minute 'response' target circular and giving Provider unilateral control of the clock start. 04_sla.md cl.5.4

BCDR objectives conflict with SLA targets: RTO of 8 hours from Invocation exceeds the 4-hour Priority 1 Resolution target, and up to 12 further hours of failback unavailability is permitted. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.2; 04_sla.md cl.5.1

Availability exclusion conflict: BCDR excludes all Continuity Event and failback downtime from the availability calculation and suspends SLA obligations entirely, but the SLA excludes only agreed maintenance windows and lists no continuity exclusion. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1, 5.3; 04_sla.md cl.3.3, 9

Service credits applied automatically to the next invoice amount to a deduction from sums due, contrary to the MSA's prohibition on set-off, counterclaim, deduction or withholding. 04_sla.md cl.4.1; 01_msa.md cl.4.5

'Sole financial remedy' conflict: the SLA makes service credits the sole financial remedy for availability failures, while the SOW grants separate credits and the MSA/DPA preserve general damages and disapply limitations. 04_sla.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1

No mechanism for calculating service credits: neither the SOW nor the SLA states how a credit is computed for a given availability shortfall, only caps (25% and 10%). 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.1–4.2
'Named key personnel' cannot be substituted without consent, but no key personnel are named anywhere in the contract set, so the protection is inoperable. 02_sow.md cl.3.5

The 'DPA — PRECEDENCE' clause states only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement and sets no precedence rule, despite the DPA containing terms that contradict the MSA; the heading promises a rule that is absent. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

Remediation timescales inconsistent within the Information Security Policy: critical penetration-test findings must be fixed within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 and 9.1

The DPA's mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is inconsistent with the DPA's own disapplication of all liability limits and with the MSA cap, and purports to shift statutory fines in a way that cuts across MSA 13. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1–11.2; 01_msa.md cl.13

Document set is internally mislabelled: the first four documents are headed 'DOCUMENT n of 4' but nine documents are supplied (Order Form, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure, Exit Plan), so the set's own numbering and any 'entire agreement' understanding of its contents are wrong. The Order Form's precedence list omits itself from the ranked categories in a coherent way and does not address the Schedules that expressly claim priority (SOW 1.2), leaving Schedule-versus-Order Form conflicts unresolved. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1(c); 02_sow.md cl.1.2

Phase durations (3 + 15 + 12 + 6 = 36 months) cannot be shortened because phases may overlap only by written agreement, so the programme necessarily outruns the contract term in both the MSA and Order Form. 02_sow.md cl.4.1–4.5; 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Delivery lead must be available during Customer's (UK) working hours while the whole team operates from Bengaluru, with no time-zone or coverage provision reconciling this with 24x7 Priority 1 support. 02_sow.md cl.3.3–3.4; 04_sla.md cl.2.1
Assumption that no more than three legacy interfaces need bespoke adapters has no stated consequence or change mechanism if exceeded, leaving scope and price open. 02_sow.md cl.10.3

Order Form allows invoices without a valid purchase order number to be returned unpaid, which conflicts with the MSA/SOW obligation to pay undisputed invoices within a fixed period and provides no cure timetable. 05_order_form.md cl.5.3; 01_msa.md cl.4.3

findings: Circular precedence: MSA clause 14.2 states the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1.2 states the SOW (which is Schedule 1) prevails over the MSA. Each document claims priority over the other and there is no tie-breaker. 01_msa.md §14.2 vs 02_sow.md §1.2

Three-way precedence conflict: the Order Form claims to rank above everything and places the MSA second, the MSA claims to prevail over all Schedules/Addenda, and the SOW claims to prevail over the MSA. The resulting ranking is circular and unresolvable. 05_order_form.md §2.1–2.2 vs 01_msa.md §14.2 vs 02_sow.md §1.2

The Order Form is neither a 'Schedule' (MSA 1.6 requires a document expressly stated to be a Schedule) nor an 'Addendum', so on the MSA's own definition of 'Agreement' (1.1) the Order Form is not part of the Agreement at all, yet it purports to be the highest-ranking document. 05_order_form.md §2 vs 01_msa.md §1.1, §1.6

No rule governs conflicts between two Schedules of equal rank (e.g. SOW/Schedule 1 vs SLA/Schedule 2 on availability and service credits; SLA vs BCDR on suspension of service levels). The precedence scheme is incomplete. 01_msa.md §14, 05_order_form.md §2.1(c)

'Business Day' is defined twice and incompatibly: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays in the MSA, but Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays in the SLA. The SLA definition also contradicts SOW 1.3 (MSA definitions apply) and the England and Wales governing law. 01_msa.md §1.2 vs 04_sla.md §1.1
Monthly Fee stated as two different amounts: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW. 01_msa.md §4.1 vs 02_sow.md §5.1
Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800 (the SOW figure) and is inconsistent with the MSA's £12,400 monthly Fee (£148,800 per year). 05_order_form.md §1.4 vs 01_msa.md §4.1

Three inconsistent payment terms for the same invoices: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md §4.3 vs 02_sow.md §5.3 vs 05_order_form.md §1.6
Initial term conflict: MSA provides a 24-month initial term while the Order Form provides a 12-month initial term for the same services. 01_msa.md §3.1 vs 05_order_form.md §1.2

The SOW commits Provider to a 36-month programme (phases totalling 3+15+12+6 = 36 months) which cannot be completed within either the 24-month MSA initial term or the 12-month Order Form initial term. 02_sow.md §2.1, §4 vs 01_msa.md §3.1 and 05_order_form.md §1.2

Start-date conflict: the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027) and the Order Form Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027), and before the Order Form signature date of 12 March 2027 — obligations begin before the contract exists. 02_sow.md §2.2 vs 01_msa.md Effective Date and 05_order_form.md §1.3, §7.3

Termination notice periods irreconcilable: 90 days for convenience under the MSA, 30 days for convenience under the SOW, and 30 days non-renewal notice under the Order Form (against the MSA's 12-month auto-renewal terminable only under clause 3.3's 90-day notice). 01_msa.md §3.2–3.3 vs 02_sow.md §2.3 vs 05_order_form.md §6.1–6.2

Acceptance mechanism conflict: MSA 6.1 provides that no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer expressly confirms in writing, while SOW 6.3 deems a Deliverable accepted by Customer's silence after 5 Business Days. Both cannot operate. 01_msa.md §6.1 vs 02_sow.md §6.3

Reference to a non-existent provision: MSA 6.2 requires assessment against acceptance criteria 'set out in Schedule 1, Section 12', but Statement of Work 1 has only 10 sections and contains no acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md §6.2 vs 02_sow.md

No acceptance criteria exist anywhere: the SOW leaves Deliverables to a 'phase plan maintained by the delivery lead' (a unilateral document), so the MSA warranty that Deliverables conform to 'the applicable acceptance criteria' has no measurable content. 02_sow.md §6.1 vs 01_msa.md §6.2, §8.2
Availability target stated twice and inconsistently: not less than 99.5% in the SOW and not less than 99.9% in the SLA for the same platform. 02_sow.md §7.2 vs 04_sla.md §3.1
Service credit cap conflict: up to 25% of the monthly Fee under the SOW versus a maximum of 10% of the monthly Fee under the SLA. 02_sow.md §7.4 vs 04_sla.md §4.2
No method for calculating service credits is given in any document (only caps of 'up to' 25%/10%), so the credit entitlement is unquantifiable. 02_sow.md §7.4 and 04_sla.md §4

Service level start date conflict: SOW says service levels begin at the start of Phase 3 (roughly month 19), the Order Form says they apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md §7.1 vs 05_order_form.md §3.3

Support coverage conflict: the SLA provides 08:00–18:00 Business Day cover for Priority 2 and 3, whereas the Order Form provides 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md §2.2 vs 05_order_form.md §3.1

Automatic credit application on the next invoice conflicts with the MSA prohibition on set-off, deduction or withholding without Provider's written agreement, and 'sole financial remedy' also sits uneasily with the MSA's general damages regime. 04_sla.md §4.1, §4.3 vs 01_msa.md §4.5, §13.1

Liability cap conflict: the MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees (about £153,600) and states that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW sets a £250,000 cap for Provider. 01_msa.md §13.1, §13.3 vs 02_sow.md §9.2

The DPA disapplies all limitations and exclusions of liability for any breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law, directly contradicting the MSA's statement that its cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of any Schedule or Addendum. 03_dpa.md §11.1 vs 01_msa.md §13.3

Indemnity is drafted backwards/circularly: each party indemnifies the other against fines imposed 'on it' as a result of 'the other's' breach, meaning the innocent party's fines are borne by the innocent party. Unworkable as written. 03_dpa.md §11.2
Insurance requirement conflict: £5,000,000 professional indemnity limit in the MSA versus £2,000,000 in the SOW. 01_msa.md §16.1 vs 02_sow.md §9.4

Governing law conflict: the MSA is governed by the laws of England and Wales with exclusive English jurisdiction, while the DPA states it is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md §15 vs 03_dpa.md §13.2

Internally self-defeating clause: DPA 13.1 says the Addendum is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement 'save as provided in clause 13.2', but 13.2 substitutes a different law for the whole Addendum, leaving 13.1 with no effect. 03_dpa.md §13.1–13.2

Audit rights conflict: the MSA states Customer has 'no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems' beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, whereas the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2 vs 03_dpa.md §9.1–9.2

MSA 12.2 makes Provider's records available 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 abolishes inspection rights and provides only a SOC 2 report — so clause 12.2 grants nothing and contradicts itself. 01_msa.md §12.2 with §10.2

Subcontracting conflict: the MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md §9.3 vs 03_dpa.md §5.1

'Confidential Information' conflict: the MSA limits it to information marked confidential at the time of disclosure, while the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked. 01_msa.md §11.1 vs 03_dpa.md §1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination, yet Provider must retain records and data for 7 years — for four years data is held with no confidentiality obligation attaching. 01_msa.md §11.3 vs §12.4

Retention versus deletion conflict: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years after termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention for 90 days then deletion. These three obligations cannot all be satisfied. 01_msa.md §12.4 vs 03_dpa.md §8.2 vs 09_exit.md §2.3, §5.2
Security log retention of 18 months followed by deletion conflicts with the MSA's 7-year retention obligation for all records relating to the Agreement. 06_infosec.md §5.2 vs 01_msa.md §12.4

Retention of service reports and the change log only 'for the duration of the Agreement' conflicts with the MSA requirement to retain records for 7 years after expiry or termination. 04_sla.md §6.3 and 08_change_control.md §9.3 vs 01_msa.md §12.4

'Security Incident' is defined twice and incompatibly: broadly in the DPA (any unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction) and narrowly in the SLA (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of data). 03_dpa.md §1.6 vs 04_sla.md §7.1

Three inconsistent security incident notification deadlines for the same event: 24 hours (DPA), 72 hours (SLA), 48 hours (Information Security Policy). 03_dpa.md §6.1 vs 04_sla.md §7.3 vs 06_infosec.md §6.1

Reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum' for security escalation contacts, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md §7.4 vs 03_dpa.md Annexes

The 'nominated security contact' referred to for incident notification is not identified or provided for in any document (the Order Form names only commercial and technical contacts). 04_sla.md §7.3 vs 05_order_form.md §4

Reference to a non-existent clause: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17', but the MSA ends at clause 16 and establishes no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md §4.1 vs 01_msa.md

Reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan states Provider's personal data obligations are in 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14', but the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md §5.3 vs 03_dpa.md

Broken cross-reference: the Change Control Procedure charges impact-assessment preparation 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', but the Exit Plan contains only a transition assistance day rate (£1,250) and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md §7.2 vs 09_exit.md §3.2

Change approval conflict: the MSA requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, whereas the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 01_msa.md §2.4 vs 08_change_control.md §4.2, §4.3, §6.1

Change-related charges are expressly exempted from the notice requirements for charge increases, allowing circumvention of the MSA's once-per-12-months, CPI-capped uplift regime and 60-day notice. 08_change_control.md §5.3 vs 01_msa.md §4.4

Internal timing contradiction: escalation of a change disagreement allows up to three levels of 5 Business Days each (15 Business Days) while expressly not suspending the timetable, yet the Change Request is deemed approved if Customer does not respond within 10 Business Days — a change can be deemed approved while the dispute over it is still being escalated. 08_change_control.md §4.2, §8.1–8.3

Data location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations, but the SOW places the delivery team (who require system access) in Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa.md §4.1, §4.3, Annex 2 vs 02_sow.md §3.4

The Information Security Policy allows Customer data to be stored in any Provider region as determined by Provider's CISO, with notification of new regions up to 30 days after they enter service — directly contradicting the DPA requirement for prior written Customer authorisation and a transfer mechanism. 06_infosec.md §2.1, §2.3 vs 03_dpa.md §4.1–4.2

The BCDR recovery site is Frankfurt, Germany, which is not among the DPA's approved processing locations (London primary, Dublin disaster recovery); the DPA Annex 2 DR site and the BCDR DR site are different. 07_bcdr.md §3.1 vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Encryption-at-rest conflict: the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, but the Policy requires encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data', and ordinary personal data (contact details, transaction records, loyalty identifiers) falls into the unencrypted 'Internal Data' class. 06_infosec.md §1.2–1.3, §3.1 vs 03_dpa.md §7.2

Recovery objectives conflict with service level targets: an 8-hour RTO (plus up to 12 hours of unavailability on return to primary) is irreconcilable with a Priority 1 Resolution target of 4 hours and with 99.9% monthly availability (about 43 minutes of permitted downtime per month). 07_bcdr.md §2.1, §5.2 vs 04_sla.md §3.1, §5.1

BCDR suspends all obligations under the SLA for the duration of a Continuity Event (including Priority 1 support and status obligations), while the SLA's own exclusions list (clause 9) does not recognise Continuity Events at all — two inconsistent treatments of the same outage. 07_bcdr.md §5.1, §5.3 vs 04_sla.md §9

Circular/meaningless measurement: response and resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the response target can never be breached and Provider controls the clock start. 04_sla.md §5.4

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services until 6 months after the effective date of termination, which contradicts the fixed terms and immediate-termination right for material breach, and conflicts with the DPA's 30-day post-termination deletion obligation. 09_exit.md §2.1–2.2 vs 01_msa.md §3.1, §3.4 and 03_dpa.md §8.2

Data return format conflict: the Exit Plan requires return of Customer data 'in the format used by Provider's systems', while the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md §4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md §8.1

Provider's exit obligations are made conditional on Customer approving Provider's effort estimate before assistance begins, creating a deadlock that can defeat the mandatory handover obligations in clause 4.1. 09_exit.md §3.4 vs §3.1, §4.1

Provider must make its Delivery Lead and a solution architect available for knowledge transfer during a transition period that may extend beyond the programme and the term, with no obligation to retain those roles after the SOW terminates. 09_exit.md §6.1 vs 02_sow.md §2.3, §3.1
SOW prohibits substituting 'named key personnel' but no key personnel are named in the SOW, Order Form or any other document, so the restriction has no subject matter. 02_sow.md §3.5

The MSA requires Customer to nominate a single point of contact, while the Order Form names two separate Customer contacts (commercial and technical) plus a security contact is referred to elsewhere. 01_msa.md §5.2 vs 05_order_form.md §4.1–4.2
Clause headed 'PRECEDENCE' contains no precedence rule at all, leaving the DPA's rank relative to the MSA and Schedules unstated despite the conflicts between them. 03_dpa.md §12

The Information Security Policy requires an incident register to be made available at a 'quarterly security review', but no quarterly security review is established in the governance provisions (which provide only a monthly service review and a quarterly steering committee). 06_infosec.md §6.3 vs 02_sow.md §8

Internal inconsistency in remediation timing: critical penetration test findings must be remediated within 30 days, while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for a critical finding requiring a patch. 06_infosec.md §7.4 vs §9.1
Assumption that no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters has no stated consequence or remedy if exceeded, leaving scope and charges undetermined. 02_sow.md §10.3

Document set is internally mislabelled: the headers state 'DOCUMENT 1 of 4' through 'DOCUMENT 4 of 4' yet nine documents are included (Documents 5–9 carry no 'of' count), so the contract set's own inventory is wrong. Headers of 01_msa.md–04_sla.md vs 05_order_form.md–09_exit.md

Exit milestones are measured from the effective date of termination (T) while the transition period begins on the date notice is given, so milestone timing is disconnected from the period during which assistance is owed; milestone 5 ('End of transition period') is also undated relative to T. 09_exit.md Annex 1 vs §2.1

The MSA requires Provider to comply with Customer's reasonable instructions on the manner of performance, while the DPA restricts Provider to processing only on Customer's documented instructions and requires Provider to challenge infringing instructions — the two instruction regimes are unreconciled. 01_msa.md §2.3 vs 03_dpa.md §2.2–2.3

'Fee' is defined in the MSA as amounts payable under clause 4 (£12,400), but service credits, liability caps and the Order Form ACV are all calculated on the SOW figure (£12,800), so every Fee-derived calculation is ambiguous. 01_msa.md §1.4, §4.1 vs 02_sow.md §5.1, 04_sla.md §4.2, 01_msa.md §13.1

findings: Circular precedence: the MSA states that the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 (Schedule 1) states that the SOW prevails over the MSA, and the Order Form states that it prevails over everything. The three clauses cannot all operate. MSA cl. 14.2; SOW cl. 1.2; Order Form cl. 2.1–2.2

The Order Form claims top precedence and is described as being 'under the Master Services Agreement', but it is neither a 'Schedule' nor an 'Addendum' as defined, so it falls outside the definition of 'Agreement' and outside the MSA precedence clause altogether. MSA cl. 1.1, 1.6, 14.2; Order Form cl. 2.1

Precedence internally inconsistent within the Order Form: cl. 2.1 sets a four-tier ranking with the MSA above Schedules, while cl. 2.2 gives the Order Form absolute priority; and cl. 2.1 does not account for the SOW's own priority claim. Order Form cl. 2.1 vs 2.2

The DPA's 'Precedence' clause says only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement and provides no conflict rule, leaving DPA-specific terms (audit, liability, data location) to be overridden by MSA cl. 14.2. DPA cl. 12.1
Conflicting monthly Fee: £12,400 in the MSA versus £12,800 in the SOW for the same Services. MSA cl. 4.1 vs SOW cl. 5.1
Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800, matching the SOW but contradicting the MSA fee of £12,400 (£148,800 per year). Order Form cl. 1.4 vs MSA cl. 4.1
Three irreconcilable payment terms: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). MSA cl. 4.3; SOW cl. 5.3; Order Form cl. 1.6

Conflicting initial terms: 24 months (MSA), 12 months from Service Commencement Date (Order Form), and a 36-month programme (SOW) that cannot complete within either. MSA cl. 3.1; Order Form cl. 1.2; SOW cl. 2.1

The SOW programme commences 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA Effective Date of 1 April 2027 and before the Order Form Service Commencement Date, i.e. work starts before the contract exists. SOW cl. 2.2 vs MSA Effective Date; Order Form cl. 1.3
The Order Form is dated 12 March 2027, after the 1 March 2027 programme start date in the SOW. Order Form cl. 7.3 vs SOW cl. 2.2

Conflicting termination/non-renewal notice periods: 90 days for convenience (MSA), 30 days for the SOW, and 30 days non-renewal (Order Form). A Customer giving 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form would breach the MSA requirement. MSA cl. 3.3; SOW cl. 2.3; Order Form cl. 6.2

Deemed acceptance conflict: the MSA prohibits any deemed acceptance and requires express written acceptance, while the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. MSA cl. 6.1 vs SOW cl. 6.3
Broken cross-reference: acceptance criteria are said to be in 'Schedule 1, Section 12', but the SOW (Schedule 1) contains only 10 sections and sets out no acceptance criteria. MSA cl. 6.2

No acceptance criteria exist anywhere: the SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the Provider's delivery lead, so the MSA warranty of conformity 'to the applicable acceptance criteria' has no measurable content and the Deliverables list is unilaterally controlled by Provider. MSA cl. 8.2; SOW cl. 6.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA extinguishes any right to audit, inspect or attend Provider premises/systems beyond receipt of a SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems. MSA cl. 10.2 vs DPA cl. 9.1–9.2

Internal contradiction: Provider must make records available to Customer on reasonable request 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes all inspection rights and only requires delivery of a SOC 2 report. MSA cl. 12.1–12.2 vs cl. 10.2

Conflicting liability caps: MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees (~£149k–£154k) and states that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000. MSA cl. 13.1, 13.3 vs SOW cl. 9.2

The DPA states that no limitation of liability in the Agreement applies to breach of the DPA or Data Protection Law, which is irreconcilable with the MSA cap that expressly overrides Schedules and Addenda (and with MSA cl. 14.2 giving the MSA priority). DPA cl. 11.1 vs MSA cl. 13.1, 13.3, 14.2
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance limits: £5,000,000 in the MSA versus £2,000,000 in the SOW. MSA cl. 16.1 vs SOW cl. 9.4

'Business Day' defined two incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA), the latter also inconsistent with an English-law, UK-based contract. MSA cl. 1.2 vs SLA cl. 1.1
Conflicting availability commitments for the same platform: 99.5% per month (SOW) versus 99.9% per month (SLA). SOW cl. 7.2 vs SLA cl. 3.1
Conflicting service credit caps: up to 25% of the monthly Fee (SOW) versus a maximum of 10% of the monthly Fee (SLA). SOW cl. 7.4 vs SLA cl. 4.2

Conflicting start of service levels: from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme) under the SOW versus from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) under the Order Form. SOW cl. 7.1 vs Order Form cl. 3.3

Under the SOW timetable Phase 3 begins around September/October 2029, after the expiry of the Order Form initial term (and after the MSA 24-month initial term), so the service-level regime would never take effect within the contracted term. SOW cl. 4.1–4.3, 7.1; Order Form cl. 1.2; MSA cl. 3.1
Conflicting support coverage: 24x7 for all priority levels (Order Form) versus Priority 2 and 3 support only 08:00–18:00 on Business Days (SLA). Order Form cl. 3.1 vs SLA cl. 2.2

'Security Incident' defined two incompatible ways: any unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction (DPA) versus only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of data (SLA); the InfoSec Policy uses a third formulation ('confirmed security incident'). DPA cl. 1.6 vs SLA cl. 7.1 vs InfoSec cl. 6.1

Three conflicting security-incident notification deadlines for the same event: 24 hours (DPA), 72 hours (SLA), 48 hours (InfoSec Policy). They cannot all be complied with. DPA cl. 6.1; SLA cl. 7.3; InfoSec cl. 6.1

Internal inconsistency in the SLA: a Security Incident is treated as a Priority 1 Incident requiring 15-minute response and 4-hour resolution, yet notification to Customer is allowed to take up to 72 hours. SLA cl. 7.2 vs 7.3
Reference to a non-existent annex: escalation contacts are said to be listed in 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum', but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. SLA cl. 7.4
Reference to a non-existent clause: the DPA has only 13 clauses, so the cross-reference to 'Data Processing Addendum, clause 14' is broken. Exit Plan cl. 5.3
Reference to a non-existent clause and body: the MSA has 16 clauses and no Change Control Board, so the reference to 'the Master Services Agreement, clause 17' is broken. Change Control cl. 4.1

Internal contradiction on governing law within the DPA: cl. 13.1 applies the law of the Agreement (England and Wales) 'save as provided in clause 13.2', while cl. 13.2 applies the law of the Republic of Ireland to the whole Addendum, negating cl. 13.1. DPA cl. 13.1 vs 13.2

The DPA's Irish governing law conflicts with the MSA's English governing law and exclusive English jurisdiction clause (and no carve-out from exclusive jurisdiction is provided). DPA cl. 13.2 vs MSA cl. 15.1–15.2

Data location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA with approved locations of London and Dublin only, while the SOW places the delivery team (which will access data) in Bengaluru, India. DPA cl. 4.1, 4.3, Annex 2 vs SOW cl. 3.4

The InfoSec Policy permits storage and processing in any Provider region as determined unilaterally by Provider's CISO, with notice up to 30 days after a new region enters service, contradicting the DPA's requirement of prior written Customer authorisation and a fixed approved-location list. InfoSec cl. 2.1, 2.3 vs DPA cl. 4.1–4.3, Annex 2

The BCDR Plan puts the secondary recovery environment in Frankfurt, Germany, whereas DPA Annex 2 lists Dublin as the disaster recovery location and does not include Frankfurt. BCDR cl. 3.1 vs DPA Annex 2

Subcontracting conflict: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. MSA cl. 9.3 vs DPA cl. 5.1

Response and Resolution clocks run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own service management tool, which makes the 15-minute 'response' target circular and lets Provider control the start of all clocks regardless of when Customer reports the Incident. SLA cl. 5.4 with 5.1–5.3

Priority 2 resolution 'within one (1) Business Day' is indeterminate because Priority 2 support is only available 08:00–18:00 on Business Days and 'Business Day' is defined differently in the MSA and the SLA. SLA cl. 5.2, 2.2, 1.1
The SOW prohibits substitution of 'named key personnel' but no key personnel are named anywhere in the contract set (only roles are listed), making the restriction unenforceable. SOW cl. 3.5, 3.2

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, which is inconsistent with the MSA term/termination provisions (services end on termination) and provides no charging basis for that period. Exit Plan cl. 2.1–2.2 vs MSA cl. 3.3–3.4, 4.1

Exit assistance cannot begin until Customer approves Provider's effort estimate, which Provider need only supply within 15 Business Days of request; this makes the Annex 1 milestone of confirming the exit plan at T+15 Business Days and the data extract at T+30 Business Days unachievable in practice. Exit Plan cl. 3.3–3.4 vs Annex 1 milestones 1–2

Exit milestones are measured from the effective date of termination while the transition period is defined as starting on the date notice is given, so the two timelines are not aligned. Exit Plan Annex 1 (T definition) vs cl. 2.1

Internal inconsistency in remediation timing: critical penetration-test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no reconciliation of overlapping critical items. InfoSec cl. 7.4 vs 9.1

'Statement of Work' is used throughout but never defined in the MSA definitions, and 'Fee' is defined as amounts payable under MSA clause 4 even though the operative Fee is set in the SOW and Order Form. MSA cl. 1.4, 1.5, 2.1

Schedules 2–6 are stated to be Schedules but contain no evidence of execution by both parties, so they may fail the MSA's definition of 'Schedule' (a document executed by both parties) and thus fall outside the Agreement. MSA cl. 1.6 vs SLA/InfoSec/BCDR/Change Control/Exit Plan headers

Document numbering is wrong: the headers state 'DOCUMENT 1 of 4' through 'DOCUMENT 4 of 4' while the set actually contains nine documents (Documents 5–9 are unnumbered as to total). Headers of all documents

The DPA states that Annex 1 sets out the processing details 'in full', but Annex 1 omits the nature of the processing operations, security measures and any list of approved Subprocessors, duplicating rather than completing cl. 3.1–3.3. DPA cl. 3.4 and Annex 1

Indirect/consequential loss is excluded only in the SOW, while the MSA (which prevails) contains no such exclusion, creating uncertainty as to whether the exclusion applies to the Services at all. SOW cl. 9.3 vs MSA cl. 13

Invoices may be returned unpaid for lack of a valid purchase order number, which conflicts with the MSA/SOW obligation to pay each undisputed invoice within a fixed period of receipt and creates an open-ended payment escape. Order Form cl. 5.3 vs MSA cl. 4.3, SOW cl. 5.3

Provider must comply with Customer's reasonable instructions on the manner of performance, but the DPA also requires Provider to process personal data only on documented instructions while the MSA denies Customer any inspection right to verify compliance — obligations that cannot be jointly assured. MSA cl. 2.3, 10.2 vs DPA cl. 2.2

Governing law conflict, both internal and cross-document: DPA cl.13.1 adopts the law of the Agreement while cl.13.2 imposes Republic of Ireland law, and the MSA specifies English law with exclusive English jurisdiction. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1–13.2; 01_msa.md cl.15.1–15.2

Record/data retention obligations cannot all be met: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; DPA requires deletion of all personal data within 30 days of termination; Exit Plan requires 90-day retention then deletion. 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3, 5.2
InfoSec Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months, contradicting the MSA's 7-year retention of all records relating to the Agreement. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2; 01_msa.md cl.12.4
SLA requires retention of service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, contradicting the 7-year post-termination retention obligation. 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Confidentiality conflict: MSA protects only information marked confidential at disclosure, whereas the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; the MSA's 3-year survival period also conflicts with indefinite personal-data protection and 7-year retention. 01_msa.md cl.11.1, 11.3; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Subcontracting conflict: MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md cl.9.3; 03_dpa.md cl.5.1

Change process conflict: MSA requires every change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 01_msa.md cl.2.4; 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Change Control escalation is self-defeating: a Change Request is deemed approved after 10 Business Days of Customer silence, yet each of three escalation levels has 5 Business Days and escalation does not suspend the timetable, so a disputed change can be deemed approved while escalation is still running. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 8.1–8.3

Change-related charges are exempted from the notice requirements for charge increases, circumventing the MSA's once-per-12-months, 60-day-notice, CPI-capped uplift mechanism. 08_change_control.md cl.5.3; 01_msa.md cl.4.4

SLA response-time targets are circular and unmeasurable: response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute/2-hour 'response' targets measure nothing. 04_sla.md cl.5.1–5.4

Availability targets are mathematically incompatible with the BCDR objectives: 99.9% monthly availability permits about 43 minutes of downtime, while the RTO permits 8 hours plus up to 12 further hours of unavailability on return to primary. 04_sla.md cl.3.1; 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.2

Exclusion conflict: the BCDR Plan purports to exclude Continuity Event and failback downtime from the availability calculation and to suspend SLA obligations, but the SLA excludes only agreed maintenance windows and its own listed exclusions do not cover Continuity Events. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1–5.3; 04_sla.md cl.3.3, 9.1–9.3

Notice conflict: SLA requires 5 Business Days' notice of any maintenance window, which cannot be given for the up-to-12-hour failback outage contemplated by the BCDR Plan. 04_sla.md cl.3.4; 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2

Encryption conflict: DPA requires encryption of Customer Personal Data at rest, but the InfoSec Policy requires at-rest encryption only for 'Restricted Data', leaving personal data classified as Internal Data unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2; 06_infosec.md cl.1.2–1.3, 3.1

Remediation timetables inconsistent: critical penetration-test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no reconciliation of the two critical-severity regimes. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4, 9.1

InfoSec Policy allows Provider to review and materially change a contractual Schedule unilaterally, subject only to notification, contradicting the requirement for changes to be agreed in writing by both parties. 06_infosec.md cl.10.1–10.2; 01_msa.md cl.2.4

Service credits mechanism conflicts with the MSA's no-set-off/no-deduction clause and with the SoW's discretionary 'up to 25%' entitlement; the SoW also provides no formula for calculating credits. 04_sla.md cl.4.1; 01_msa.md cl.4.5; 02_sow.md cl.7.4

SLA states service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failure, which conflicts with the DPA's disapplication of all liability limits and with the general liability regime in the MSA/SoW. 04_sla.md cl.4.3; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1; 01_msa.md cl.13.1

Exit Plan obligations are internally impossible: data must be deleted after the 90-day retention period, yet handover (including delivery of all Customer data) is certified only at the end of a six-month transition period, and Annex 1 milestone 4 (parallel running) falls at T+90 Business Days, i.e. after the 90-calendar-day retention window. 09_exit.md cl.2.1, 2.3, 4.1, 5.2 and Annex 1

Exit data-return format conflicts with the DPA: Exit Plan requires return 'in the format used by Provider's systems' whereas the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a); 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, which cannot be reconciled with the MSA's fixed term, its right of immediate termination for material breach, or the DPA's 30-day post-termination deletion duty. 09_exit.md cl.1.2, 2.1–2.2; 01_msa.md cl.3.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2

Transition assistance is conditional on Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, allowing the mandatory exit obligation to stall; the 15-Business-Day estimate period also makes Annex 1 milestone 1 (T+15 Business Days) unachievable. 09_exit.md cl.3.3–3.4 and Annex 1 milestone 1

Inconsistent time baselines in the Exit Plan: the transition period runs from the date notice is given (cl.2.1) but all Annex 1 milestones run from 'T = effective date of termination'. 09_exit.md cl.2.1 and Annex 1

Order Form permits invoices without a valid PO number to be 'returned unpaid', conflicting with the unconditional obligation to pay undisputed invoices and the no-deduction clause. 05_order_form.md cl.5.3; 01_msa.md cl.4.3, 4.5

Order Form Annual Contract Value of £153,600 covers only the 12-month initial term and is inconsistent with the 36-month SoW programme scope it purports to price, and with the MSA fee figure. 05_order_form.md cl.1.1, 1.4

Document set is mislabelled: Documents 1–4 are each headed 'DOCUMENT n of 4' although the set contains nine documents (5–9 carry no 'of' count), leaving it unclear which documents form the agreement. Headers of 01_msa.md, 02_sow.md, 03_dpa.md, 04_sla.md vs 05–09

Mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is likely unenforceable and, combined with the disapplication of all liability limits, leaves uncapped exposure inconsistent with the negotiated caps elsewhere. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1–11.2

DPA precedence clause is silent on conflicts: it states only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement, leaving its data-protection terms subordinate to the MSA under MSA cl.14.2 despite DPA cl.11.1 purporting to override the MSA's liability regime. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1; 01_msa.md cl.14.2

Change Control Procedure governs changes to 'acceptance criteria' that no document contains, and the £35,000 Delivery Lead approval threshold is unbounded in aggregate (no cap on the number of such changes). 08_change_control.md cl.1.1, 4.3

BCDR Plan excludes simultaneous loss of primary and recovery environments and depends on an unnamed third-party infrastructure supplier, leaving the RTO/RPO commitments effectively unsupported, with no linkage to the SLA exclusions. 07_bcdr.md cl.8.1–8.2

A Security Incident is deemed a Priority 1 Incident requiring Resolution within 4 hours under the SLA, which is inconsistent with the DPA's incident regime (24-hour notification, no resolution target) and with the InfoSec Policy's 48-hour/10-Business-Day reporting cycle. 04_sla.md cl.7.2, 5.1; 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1–6.2
unmatched: Warranty in MSA cl.8.2 is unworkable because it measures conformity against 'applicable acceptance criteria' which no document actually specifies. 01_msa.md cl.8.2

Broken cross-reference: Change Control Procedure charges impact-assessment preparation 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', but the Exit Plan contains only a transition-assistance day rate and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2; 09_exit.md cl.3.2

Deliverables are undefined in substance: MSA defines 'Deliverable' as an item identified in a Statement of Work, but the SoW defers identification to a phase plan unilaterally maintained by Provider's delivery lead. 01_msa.md cl.1.3; 02_sow.md cl.6.1
SLA requires retention of service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, contradicting the 7-year post-termination retention obligation. 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 01_msa.md cl.12.4

SLA response-time targets are circular and unmeasurable: response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute/2-hour 'response' targets measure nothing. 04_sla.md cl.5.1–5.4

The Order Form claims highest precedence but is not a 'Schedule' or 'Addendum' and is therefore not part of the 'Agreement' as defined; its contractual status is undefined. 05_order_form.md cl.2; 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6

Monthly Fee stated as £12,400 in the MSA but £12,800 in the SoW; the Order Form's Annual Contract Value of £153,600 (12 × £12,800) is consistent with the SoW and inconsistent with the MSA. 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4
Three incompatible payment terms: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SoW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Incompatible term lengths: MSA initial term 24 months, Order Form initial term 12 months, and a 36-month programme under the SoW that cannot be completed within either term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 02_sow.md cl.2.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

The SoW programme commences 1 March 2027, before the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027), before the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) and before the Order Form signature date (12 March 2027). 02_sow.md cl.2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3, 7.3

Inconsistent termination/non-renewal notice: 90 days for convenience under the MSA, 30 days to terminate the SoW, and 30 days' notice of non-renewal under the Order Form. 01_msa.md cl.3.3; 02_sow.md cl.2.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.2

'Business Day' defined two different ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA). The US-holiday definition is also incongruous in an England and Wales governed contract and infects every Business Day deadline in the SLA, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure and Exit Plan. 01_msa.md cl.1.2; 04_sla.md cl.1.1
Conflicting availability commitments: 99.5% monthly in the SoW versus 99.9% monthly in the SLA. 02_sow.md cl.7.2; 04_sla.md cl.3.1
Conflicting service credit caps: up to 25% of the monthly Fee (SoW) versus a hard cap of 10% (SLA). 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2

Service levels start dates conflict: from the start of Phase 3 (i.e. month 19 of the programme) under the SoW, but from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) under the Order Form. 02_sow.md cl.7.1; 05_order_form.md cl.3.3

Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels, while the SLA limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl.3.1; 04_sla.md cl.2.2
Service credits applied automatically as a deduction from the next invoice conflict with the MSA prohibition on set-off, deduction or withholding. 04_sla.md cl.4.1; 01_msa.md cl.4.5

'Service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy' for availability failures conflicts with the SoW credit regime, with the MSA's general liability regime and with the DPA statement that no limitation of liability applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. 04_sla.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.13; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1

'Security Incident' defined two irreconcilable ways: broad (any unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of personal data) in the DPA versus narrow (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption) in the SLA. 03_dpa.md cl.1.6; 04_sla.md cl.7.1

Three conflicting security incident notification deadlines: 24 hours (DPA), 72 hours (SLA), 48 hours (InfoSec Policy). They cannot all be satisfied and no document subordinates the others. 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 04_sla.md cl.7.3; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1

Internal inconsistency: a Security Incident is deemed a Priority 1 Incident (15-minute response, 4-hour resolution) yet notification to Customer is allowed to take up to 72 hours. 04_sla.md cl.7.2 vs cl.7.3
Cross-reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum', but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4; 03_dpa.md Annexes

Cross-reference to a non-existent provision: MSA acceptance criteria are said to be in 'Schedule 1, Section 12', but the SoW has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md cl.6.2; 02_sow.md

Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: the Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board 'described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and no such board is described anywhere. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1; 01_msa.md
Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan refers to 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3; 03_dpa.md

Cross-reference to a rate that does not exist: charges for preparing an impact assessment are said to be 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', which only sets a transition assistance day rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2; 09_exit.md cl.3.2

Acceptance mechanisms are mutually exclusive: the MSA prohibits deemed acceptance and requires express written acceptance, while the SoW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. 01_msa.md cl.6.1; 02_sow.md cl.6.3

Audit rights contradicted: the MSA states the SOC 2 report satisfies assurance and Customer has 'no further right to audit, inspect or attend' Provider's premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit and inspection right. 01_msa.md cl.10.2; 03_dpa.md cl.9.1–9.2

MSA records clause makes Provider's record availability subject to clause 10.2 (which removes audit rights), rendering the record-inspection obligation self-defeating and inconsistent with the DPA audit right. 01_msa.md cl.12.2
Subcontracting conflict: the MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md cl.9.3; 03_dpa.md cl.5.1

Conflicting liability caps: MSA cap of 12 months' Fees (approx. £148,800–£153,600) stated to apply notwithstanding any Schedule, versus a £250,000 cap in the SoW, versus the DPA statement that no limitation applies at all. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md cl.9.2; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance limits: not less than £5,000,000 (MSA) versus not less than £2,000,000 (SoW). 01_msa.md cl.16.1; 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Governing law conflict and internal contradiction: the MSA imposes England and Wales law and exclusive jurisdiction; the DPA says it is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and clause 13.2 then imposes Republic of Ireland law. 01_msa.md cl.15; 03_dpa.md cl.13.1–13.2
The DPA clause headed 'Precedence' states no precedence rule, leaving the DPA subordinate to the MSA under MSA cl.14.2 and thus nullifying DPA cl.11.1. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

Irreconcilable data retention/deletion obligations: retain all records, data and materials for 7 years (MSA); delete all personal data within 30 days of termination (DPA); retain all Customer data for 90 days after termination (Exit Plan); retain security logs 18 months then delete (InfoSec); retain service reports only for the duration of the Agreement (SLA). 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3; 06_infosec.md cl.5.2; 04_sla.md cl.6.3

Data location conflict: DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA with approved locations London and Dublin, while the SoW delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India (implying access/transfer), the InfoSec Policy allows any Provider region as unilaterally determined by Provider's CISO with only 30 days' after-the-fact notice, and the BCDR recovery site is Frankfurt (not an approved location in DPA Annex 2). 03_dpa.md cl.4.1–4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md cl.3.4; 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 2.3; 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1

Encryption scope conflict: the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while the InfoSec Policy requires encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data' (personal data such as contact details and transaction records fall in the unencrypted 'Internal Data' class). 03_dpa.md cl.7.2; 06_infosec.md cl.3.1, 1.2–1.3

Confidentiality definitions conflict: the MSA requires information to be marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; MSA precedence would defeat the DPA provision. 01_msa.md cl.11.1; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination while records containing that information must be retained for 7 years, and while personal data protections are open-ended — inconsistent survival periods. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4

Change control conflicts with the MSA requirement that any change be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation: the Procedure allows deemed approval after 10 Business Days' silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1; 01_msa.md cl.2.4

Change-related charges are declared exempt from notice requirements for charge increases, which allows circumvention of the MSA's once-yearly, CPI-capped, 60-day-notice fee increase mechanism. 08_change_control.md cl.5.3; 01_msa.md cl.4.4

The Delivery Lead's £35,000 unilateral approval threshold is disproportionate to a £12,800 monthly fee and is inconsistent with the Order Form's fixed Annual Contract Value. 08_change_control.md cl.4.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4

Escalation provision states escalation 'does not suspend the timetable in clause 3', but clause 3 is Provider's own impact-assessment timetable, not the approval timetable in clause 4 in which disagreements arise — mismatched cross-reference. 08_change_control.md cl.8.3

RTO of 8 hours from Invocation is incompatible with the SLA Priority 1 Resolution target of 4 hours, and with 99.9% monthly availability (approx. 43 minutes of permitted downtime). 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1; 04_sla.md cl.3.1, 5.1

BCDR excludes continuity-event and failback unavailability (up to 12 further hours) from the availability calculation, but the SLA exclusions list only maintenance windows, Customer equipment and third-party outages — the exclusion regimes conflict. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2–5.3; 04_sla.md cl.3.3, 9

BCDR suspends all SLA obligations for the duration of a Continuity Event, contradicting the SLA's 24x7 Priority 1 support and service credit regime, and giving Provider (which alone declares Invocation) unilateral power to switch off its own service levels. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1, 4.1; 04_sla.md cl.2.1, 4

Response/Resolution clock runs from Provider's own acknowledgement in its service management tool, which makes the 'response' target circular (response measured from response) and lets Provider control the start of all targets. 04_sla.md cl.5.4

Priority 2 Resolution 'within one Business Day' is unworkable/ambiguous given Priority 2 support is only available 08:00–18:00 on Business Days and 'Business Day' is itself defined inconsistently. 04_sla.md cl.5.2 with cl.2.2, 1.1
The SoW prohibits substitution of 'named key personnel', but no key personnel are named in any document and no key-personnel annex exists. 02_sow.md cl.3.5

Deliverables are defined by the MSA as items identified in a Statement of Work, but the SoW leaves them to a 'phase plan maintained by the delivery lead' — i.e. determined unilaterally by Provider and outside the contract documents; this also leaves the IP assignment and acceptance obligations without identifiable subject matter. 02_sow.md cl.6.1; 01_msa.md cl.1.3, 7.2

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, which is irreconcilable with immediate termination for material breach, with the DPA's 30-day post-termination deletion duty, and with the 90-day data retention period (knowledge transfer at T+60 Business Days and parallel running at T+90 Business Days fall outside the 90-day retention window and before handover certification). 09_exit.md cl.1.2, 2.1–2.3, Annex 1; 01_msa.md cl.3.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2
Data return format conflict: Exit Plan requires data 'in the format used by Provider's systems' while the DPA requires a 'structured, commonly used format'. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a); 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Transition assistance is chargeable at £1,250 per person per day even though the Services continue during transition 'on the terms then in force' and the SoW Fee is stated to cover all personnel — creating double-charging ambiguity. 09_exit.md cl.2.2, 3.2; 02_sow.md cl.5.2

Provider's exit obligations are made conditional on Customer approving Provider's effort estimate before assistance begins, which permits Provider to withhold mandatory transition assistance pending a commercial agreement. 09_exit.md cl.3.1 vs cl.3.4

Change log retention 'for the duration of the Agreement' conflicts with the requirement to hand over the change log at exit and with the MSA's 7-year retention obligation. 08_change_control.md cl.9.3; 09_exit.md cl.4.1(e); 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Inconsistent critical remediation timescales within the same policy: critical penetration test findings within 30 days but critical security patches within 14 days, with no rule for overlap. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

'Restricted Data' includes payment card data, which is not among the categories of personal data described in the DPA and Annex 1 — the documents describe inconsistent data scopes. 06_infosec.md cl.1.2; 03_dpa.md cl.3.3 and Annex 1

Order Form permits invoices without a valid purchase order number to be 'returned unpaid', which conflicts with the MSA/SoW obligation to pay undisputed invoices within a fixed period and with the no-deduction clause. 05_order_form.md cl.5.3; 01_msa.md cl.4.3, 4.5

Document set is mislabelled and internally inconsistent as to its own composition: documents are headed 'DOCUMENT 1 of 4' through '4 of 4' yet the set contains nine documents (Order Form plus Schedules 3–6), and the MSA definition of 'Agreement' does not account for them. Headers of 01_msa.md–04_sla.md; 01_msa.md cl.1.1

Availability/credit regime is unquantified in the SoW: 'service credits of up to twenty-five per cent' with no calculation table, thresholds or claim mechanism, and no reconciliation with the SLA's automatic-credit mechanism. 02_sow.md cl.7.4
SoW assumption that no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters has no stated consequence or change mechanism if breached, leaving scope and price indeterminate. 02_sow.md cl.10.3
Only Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, with no deputy or alternate, creating an unworkable single point of failure in a continuity plan. 07_bcdr.md cl.4.1
Exit rehearsal required 'at least once in the term' while 'term' is itself ambiguous (24 months in the MSA, 12 months in the Order Form). 09_exit.md cl.9.2

findings: Circular/contradictory precedence: MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while Statement of Work 1 (a Schedule) says it prevails over the MSA. Each document claims priority over the other, so no conflict can be resolved. 01_msa.md cl. 14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 1.2

Third, inconsistent precedence regime: the Order Form declares itself top-ranking and ranks MSA above Schedules above Addenda, contradicting both MSA cl. 14.2 (MSA prevails over everything) and SOW cl. 1.2 (SOW prevails over MSA). 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1–2.2

The Order Form is not part of the contractual stack it purports to sit on top of: 'Agreement' is defined as the MSA plus each Schedule and Addendum only, and the Order Form is neither a Schedule (not stated to be one) nor an Addendum, so its terms have no contractual hook while simultaneously claiming highest precedence. 01_msa.md cl. 1.1 / 1.6 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 2

No tie-breaker between Schedules: Schedules 1–6 (SOW, SLA, InfoSec, BCDR, Change Control, Exit) all rank equally under the Order Form precedence list, yet they conflict with each other (e.g. availability, security incident notification, data retention), leaving conflicts unresolvable. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1(c) vs documents 02, 04, 06, 07, 09
Monthly Fee stated as £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW for the same Services. 01_msa.md cl. 4.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 5.1

Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800 (the SOW rate) and is inconsistent with the MSA rate of £12,400/month (£148,800), so the Order Form silently endorses one of two conflicting fee figures. 05_order_form.md cl. 1.4 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.1

Three mutually incompatible payment terms for the same invoices: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 5.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 1.6

Initial term conflict: MSA initial term is 24 months, the Order Form initial term is 12 months, and the SOW commits to a 36-month programme that cannot be completed within either. 01_msa.md cl. 3.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 1.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.1

The SOW programme commences 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027) and before the Order Form was signed (12 March 2027) — obligations start before the agreement exists. 02_sow.md cl. 2.2 vs 01_msa.md Effective Date and 05_order_form.md cl. 7.3
Termination-for-convenience notice periods conflict: 90 days under the MSA, 30 days under the SOW for the same Services. 01_msa.md cl. 3.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.3

Renewal/non-renewal notice conflict: MSA requires 90 days' notice to prevent automatic 12-month renewal; the Order Form requires only 30 days' notice of non-renewal. 01_msa.md cl. 3.2–3.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 6.2

Acceptance mechanism directly contradictory: the MSA prohibits deemed acceptance (express written acceptance required), while the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days of silence. 01_msa.md cl. 6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 6.3

Broken cross-reference: the MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria 'set out in Schedule 1, Section 12', but Statement of Work 1 has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md cl. 6.2 vs 02_sow.md

No acceptance criteria exist anywhere: the SOW leaves Deliverables to a 'phase plan maintained by the delivery lead' (unilaterally controlled, not contractual), yet the MSA warranty and acceptance regime depend on defined acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md cl. 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 6.2, 8.2

Audit rights irreconcilable: the MSA states Customer has no right whatsoever to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises and systems, and the InfoSec Policy lets Customer nominate a penetration-test target. 01_msa.md cl. 10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 9.1–9.2 and 06_infosec.md cl. 7.3

Internal inconsistency: MSA cl. 12.2 promises records will be made available to Customer 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes all inspection rights, so the obligation is self-cancelling. 01_msa.md cl. 12.2 vs cl. 10.2

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees (~£148,800–£153,600) and states this applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md cl. 13.1/13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 9.2

The DPA disapplies all limitations of liability for any breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law, which is irreconcilable with the MSA's statement that its cap applies notwithstanding any Addendum. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 13.3

The DPA's 'PRECEDENCE' clause states only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement and contains no conflict rule; combined with MSA cl. 14.2 the MSA prevails, nullifying DPA cll. 1.4 and 11.1. 03_dpa.md cl. 12.1

Indemnity for regulatory fines is unworkable/likely unenforceable and conflicts with the liability cap: each party indemnifies the other for fines imposed as a result of the other's breach, with no cap and no carve-out reconciliation. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 13.1
Professional indemnity insurance limit stated as not less than £5,000,000 in the MSA and not less than £2,000,000 in the SOW. 01_msa.md cl. 16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 9.4

Governing law conflict: the MSA is governed by the laws of England and Wales with exclusive English jurisdiction, while the DPA is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md cl. 15.1–15.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 13.2

Internal self-contradiction: DPA cl. 13.1 says the Addendum is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and 13.2 then overrides it entirely — the clause negates itself. 03_dpa.md cl. 13.1–13.2
Availability target conflict: 99.5% monthly availability in the SOW versus 99.9% in the SLA for the same platform. 02_sow.md cl. 7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1
Service credit cap conflict: up to 25% of the monthly Fee in the SOW versus a maximum of 10% of the monthly Fee in the SLA. 02_sow.md cl. 7.4 vs 04_sla.md cl. 4.2

Service level commencement conflict: SOW says service levels start at the beginning of Phase 3 (about month 19), while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md cl. 7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 3.3

Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels, but the SLA limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl. 3.1 vs 04_sla.md cl. 2.2

'Business Day' defined two incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA), which also imports US holidays into an English-law contract. 01_msa.md cl. 1.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 1.1

Because MSA precedence overrides the SLA's own Business Day definition, every SLA/InfoSec/BCDR/Change Control deadline expressed in Business Days is ambiguous as to which calendar applies. 04_sla.md, 06_infosec.md, 07_bcdr.md, 08_change_control.md (all Business Day references)
