Document set is internally mislabelled: documents 1–4 are headed 'DOCUMENT X of 4' although the contract set comprises nine documents (Order Form, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure and Exit Plan are unaccounted for in the stated count and in MSA cl. 14). 01_msa.md–04_sla.md headers; 01_msa.md cl. 14

Execution defect: MSA cl. 1.6 requires each Schedule to be executed by both parties, but only the Order Form contains signature blocks; Schedules 1–6 show no execution, so arguably none are part of the Agreement. 01_msa.md cl. 1.6 vs 02_sow.md, 04_sla.md, 06_infosec.md, 07_bcdr.md, 08_change_control.md, 09_exit.md

Purchase order mechanics conflict with payment terms: invoices lacking a PO number 'may be returned unpaid' with no time limit or re-issue process, undermining the fixed payment periods and the no-set-off clause. 05_order_form.md cl. 5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3, 4.5

Fee increase controls conflict: the MSA limits increases to once per 12 months on 60 days' notice capped at CPI, while the Change Control Procedure exempts change-related charges from those notice requirements and lets Provider self-approve up to £35,000 of change cost. 01_msa.md cl. 4.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl. 4.3, 5.3
Vague, unenforceable testing obligation: a 'desk-based exit rehearsal at least once in the term' with no date, scope or participation requirement, and no consequence for failure. 09_exit.md cl. 9.2

Exit milestone 5 ties handover certification to 'End of transition period' (six months after termination) while milestone 4 (parallel running) is T+90 Business Days and the transition period itself starts at notice date, mixing two different clock bases with no reconciliation. 09_exit.md Annex 1 vs cl. 2.1
unmatched: No acceptance criteria exist anywhere: the SOW leaves Deliverables to a 'phase plan maintained by the delivery lead' (unilaterally controlled, not contractual), yet the MSA warranty and acceptance regime depend on defined acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md cl. 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 6.2, 8.2

Internal inconsistency: MSA cl. 12.2 promises records will be made available to Customer 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes all inspection rights, so the obligation is self-cancelling. 01_msa.md cl. 12.2 vs cl. 10.2

Internal self-contradiction: DPA cl. 13.1 says the Addendum is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and 13.2 then overrides it entirely — the clause negates itself. 03_dpa.md cl. 13.1–13.2

Because MSA precedence overrides the SLA's own Business Day definition, every SLA/InfoSec/BCDR/Change Control deadline expressed in Business Days is ambiguous as to which calendar applies. 04_sla.md, 06_infosec.md, 07_bcdr.md, 08_change_control.md (all Business Day references)

The SLA requires notification to Customer's 'nominated security contact', but no security contact is nominated anywhere (the Order Form names only commercial and technical contacts). 04_sla.md cl. 7.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 4

Emergency changes may be implemented with no prior approval, again contradicting the MSA's absolute pre-approval requirement for changes to the Services. 08_change_control.md cl. 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 2.4
Service report retention 'for the duration of the Agreement' conflicts with the MSA's 7-year post-termination records retention obligation. 04_sla.md cl. 6.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 12.4

'Sole financial remedy' for availability failures conflicts with the SOW's separate credit entitlement and with the MSA's general liability regime (and is not carved out from DPA cl. 11.1). 04_sla.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 7.4 and 01_msa.md cl. 13.1

Circular measurement of response times: response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute/2-hour 'response' targets measure nothing and Provider controls the clock start. 04_sla.md cl. 5.4 with cl. 5.1–5.3

Contact structure conflict: the MSA requires a single Customer point of contact for the Services, while the Order Form nominates two Customer contacts (commercial and technical) and other documents assume separate security and technical contacts. 01_msa.md cl. 5.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 4 and 07_bcdr.md cl. 4.2

Transition assistance is subject to Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which allows Provider's mandatory assistance obligation to be blocked and leaves no dispute mechanism if the estimate is unreasonable. 09_exit.md cl. 3.1 vs cl. 3.4

Assumption with no consequence: the SOW assumes no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters (and that Customer documentation is accurate) but provides no mechanism, relief or change trigger if the assumption fails. 02_sow.md cl. 10.2–10.3

findings: Circular precedence: MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 (Schedule 1) says the SOW prevails over the MSA. Each document claims priority over the other, so no conflict can be resolved. 01_msa.md cl. 14.2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 1.2

Third, incompatible precedence ladder: the Order Form declares itself top of the order and states it prevails over 'any other document', contradicting both the MSA's self-priority clause and the SOW's self-priority clause. 05_order_form.md cl. 2.1–2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 14.2 and 02_sow.md cl. 1.2

The Order Form is not part of the 'Agreement' as defined (Agreement = MSA plus Schedules and Addenda only; a Schedule must be expressly stated to be a Schedule). The Order Form is neither, so its precedence clause has no contractual anchor and its terms arguably fall outside the Agreement. 01_msa.md cl. 1.1, 1.6 vs 05_order_form.md
Monthly Fee stated two different ways: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW for the same Services. 01_msa.md cl. 4.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 5.1
Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800, matching the SOW but irreconcilable with the MSA's £12,400/month (£148,800/year). 05_order_form.md cl. 1.4 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.1

Three mutually inconsistent payment terms for the same invoices: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 5.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 1.6

Three inconsistent contract durations: MSA initial term 24 months, SOW programme 36 months, Order Form initial term 12 months for the same engagement. 01_msa.md cl. 3.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 1.2

The 36-month programme (and the 36 months of phases) cannot be performed within the 24-month MSA initial term or the 12-month Order Form term without a renewal that either party can prevent on 30–90 days' notice. 02_sow.md cl. 2.1, 4.1–4.4 vs 01_msa.md cl. 3.1–3.3

Commencement dates conflict: the SOW programme starts 1 March 2027, but the MSA Effective Date and the Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027 — the SOW would begin a month before the Agreement under which it is issued exists. 02_sow.md cl. 2.2 vs 01_msa.md Effective Date and 05_order_form.md cl. 1.3

The Order Form is signed 12 March 2027, after the SOW's stated programme start date of 1 March 2027, creating a retrospective start with no backdating provision. 05_order_form.md cl. 7.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.2

Inconsistent termination/non-renewal notice periods: 90 days for convenience under the MSA, 30 days for the SOW, and 30 days non-renewal under the Order Form, with no statement of which governs the overall engagement. 01_msa.md cl. 3.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 2.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 6.2

Renewal mechanics conflict: MSA renews for successive 12-month periods terminable only on 90 days' notice, while the Order Form renews for 12-month periods with 30 days' non-renewal notice; a party giving 30 days' notice under the Order Form would still be bound by the MSA renewal. 01_msa.md cl. 3.2–3.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 6.1–6.2

'Business Day' is defined twice and incompatibly: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA). All Business Day deadlines across the documents are therefore indeterminate. 01_msa.md cl. 1.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 1.1
Availability target stated two ways for the same platform: 99.5% per month in the SOW and 99.9% per month in the SLA. 02_sow.md cl. 7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1
Service credit caps conflict: up to 25% of the monthly Fee under the SOW versus a maximum of 10% under the SLA. 02_sow.md cl. 7.4 vs 04_sla.md cl. 4.2

Service levels start on different dates: from the start of Phase 3 (approximately 18 months in) under the SOW, but from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) under the Order Form. 02_sow.md cl. 7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl. 3.3

Support coverage conflict: the Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels, while the SLA restricts Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl. 3.1 vs 04_sla.md cl. 2.1–2.2

Liability caps irreconcilable: MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees (c. £148,800–£153,600) and states the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW sets a £250,000 cap under that Schedule. 01_msa.md cl. 13.1, 13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 9.2

The DPA disapplies all limitations of liability for breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law, directly contradicting the MSA's statement that its cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of any Schedule or Addendum. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 13.3
Insurance limits conflict: professional indemnity of not less than £5,000,000 in the MSA versus not less than £2,000,000 in the SOW. 01_msa.md cl. 16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 9.4

Acceptance regimes are mutually exclusive: the MSA prohibits any deemed acceptance (express written acceptance required), while the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. 01_msa.md cl. 6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl. 6.3

Broken cross-reference: the MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria 'set out in Schedule 1, Section 12', but the SOW (Schedule 1) has only 10 sections and contains no acceptance criteria. 01_msa.md cl. 6.2

No acceptance criteria exist anywhere; Deliverables are defined only by a phase plan maintained unilaterally by Provider's delivery lead, which also conflicts with the MSA definition of Deliverable (item identified in a Statement of Work) and with the MSA warranty of conformity to 'applicable acceptance criteria'. 02_sow.md cl. 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.3, 8.2

Audit rights contradict: the MSA states Customer has no right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems beyond the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems. 01_msa.md cl. 10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 9.1–9.2

The MSA's records-access clause routes all record access through cl. 10.2 (the no-audit clause), rendering the record-keeping obligation and the DPA audit right unworkable together. 01_msa.md cl. 12.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 9

Subcontracting conflict: the MSA permits subcontracting of any part of the Services without Customer consent, whereas the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. With the MSA given priority, the DPA control is nullified. 01_msa.md cl. 9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 5.1 (and cl. 14.2)

Data location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations, but the SOW places the whole delivery team (with system access) in Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa.md cl. 4.1, Annex 2 vs 02_sow.md cl. 3.4

The Information Security Policy allows Customer data to be stored and processed in any Provider region as determined unilaterally by Provider's CISO, with notice only within 30 days after a region enters service — directly contrary to the DPA's UK/EEA restriction and its requirement for prior written authorisation and a transfer mechanism. 06_infosec.md cl. 2.1, 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 4.1–4.2

The BCDR recovery site is Frankfurt, Germany, which is not an approved processing location under DPA Annex 2 (London and Dublin only), so invoking the Plan would breach the DPA. 07_bcdr.md cl. 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 4.3, Annex 2

'Security Incident' is defined twice and inconsistently: broad definition covering any unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction (DPA) versus a narrow definition limited to confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption (SLA). 03_dpa.md cl. 1.6 vs 04_sla.md cl. 7.1

Three incompatible security-incident notification deadlines for the same event: 24 hours (DPA), 72 hours (SLA), 48 hours (Information Security Policy). 03_dpa.md cl. 6.1 vs 04_sla.md cl. 7.3 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 6.1

Internal inconsistency: a Security Incident is treated as a Priority 1 Incident requiring response in 15 minutes and Resolution in 4 hours, yet notification to Customer is permitted up to 72 hours after confirmation. 04_sla.md cl. 7.2–7.3 vs cl. 5.1
Reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum' for security escalation contacts, but the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. 04_sla.md cl. 7.4

Reference to a non-existent clause: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and describes no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl. 4.1
Reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan states Provider's personal data obligations are in 'the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl. 5.3

Change approval conflict: the MSA requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, while the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral Provider approval up to £35,000, and unapproved emergency changes. 01_msa.md cl. 2.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl. 4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Charge-increase controls conflict: the MSA limits Fee increases to once per 12 months, on 60 days' notice and capped at CPI, whereas the Change Control Procedure allows change-related charges to take effect on the next invoice free of any notice requirement, and lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve up to £35,000 of cost impact unilaterally. 01_msa.md cl. 4.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl. 4.3, 5.1, 5.3

Dangling cross-reference to a rate that does not exist: charges for preparing an impact assessment are said to be 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', but that Plan contains only a transition-assistance day rate (£1,250) and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl. 7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl. 3.2

Wrong internal cross-reference: escalation 'does not suspend the timetable in clause 3' (impact assessment), but escalation under clause 8 arises from disagreement at the approval stage in clause 4, whose deemed-approval clock is left unaddressed — a 10-Business-Day deemed approval can expire while a 3-level, 15-Business-Day escalation runs. 08_change_control.md cl. 8.1–8.3 vs cl. 4.2

Governing law contradiction within one document: clause 13.1 applies the law of the Agreement (England and Wales) 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and clause 13.2 then applies the laws of the Republic of Ireland to the same Addendum. 03_dpa.md cl. 13.1–13.2

Cross-document governing law/jurisdiction conflict: the MSA applies English law with exclusive English jurisdiction to any dispute arising out of it (including its Addenda), while the DPA applies Irish law. 01_msa.md cl. 15.1–15.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 13.2

Data retention obligations cannot all be satisfied: the MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days and deletion thereafter. 01_msa.md cl. 12.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 8.2 vs 09_exit.md cl. 2.3, 5.2

Exit timetable is internally inconsistent with the deletion/retention rules: the transition period runs 6 months after termination and handover is certified at its end (Annex 1 milestone 5), and parallel running completes at T+90 Business Days (c. 4.5 months), yet data need only be retained 90 calendar days and must be deleted 30 days after termination under the DPA. 09_exit.md cl. 2.1, 2.3, Annex 1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 8.2

Continued-service obligation conflicts with termination and deletion: Provider must keep providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, which is impossible once the Agreement has ended and Customer Personal Data has been deleted. 09_exit.md cl. 2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 3.3 and 03_dpa.md cl. 8.2

Data return format conflict: the Exit Plan requires return of Customer data 'in the format used by Provider's systems', while the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl. 4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl. 8.1

Exit deliverables include all source code and build scripts, which conflicts with the MSA reservation of Provider's pre-existing tools, methods and know-how and with the assignment of IP only in Deliverables paid for in full. 09_exit.md cl. 4.1(b) vs 01_msa.md cl. 7.2–7.3

Log retention conflict: security logs must be retained 18 months 'and then deleted', while the MSA requires all records to be retained for 7 years after termination. 06_infosec.md cl. 5.2 vs 01_msa.md cl. 12.4

Report/record retention conflicts: service reports and the change log need only be kept 'for the duration of the Agreement', contradicting the MSA's 7-year post-termination retention obligation (and the exit obligation to hand over the change log). 04_sla.md cl. 6.3 and 08_change_control.md cl. 9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 12.4 and 09_exit.md cl. 4.1(e)

Encryption scope conflict: the Information Security Policy requires encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data' (compensation, card and credential data), whereas the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, most of which would be classified as Internal Data. 06_infosec.md cl. 1.2–1.3, 3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 7.2

Confidentiality definitions conflict: the MSA protects only information marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; with the MSA given precedence, unmarked personal data loses protection. 01_msa.md cl. 11.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl. 1.4 (and cl. 14.2)

Confidentiality survives only 3 years after termination, which is shorter than the 7-year records retention obligation and inconsistent with indefinite protection of personal data under the DPA. 01_msa.md cl. 11.3 vs cl. 12.4 and 03_dpa.md cl. 1.4

Set-off prohibition conflicts with automatic service credits: Customer must pay without any set-off or deduction, yet the SLA requires Provider to apply credits automatically to the next invoice and the SOW frames credits as an entitlement. 01_msa.md cl. 4.5 vs 04_sla.md cl. 4.1 and 02_sow.md cl. 7.4

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the SOW's separate credit entitlement and with the DPA's disapplication of all liability limitations, and sits awkwardly with the MSA liability regime. 04_sla.md cl. 4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 7.4 and 03_dpa.md cl. 11.1
Recovery objectives conflict with SLA targets: RTO is 8 hours from Invocation, but a total outage is a Priority 1 Incident requiring Resolution within 4 hours. 07_bcdr.md cl. 2.1 vs 04_sla.md cl. 5.1

BCDR unilaterally suspends all SLA obligations and excludes continuity-related downtime from availability, but the SLA's exclusions list contains no such exclusion (only Customer equipment, third-party outages and maintenance windows), and the MSA/Order Form precedence rules would defeat the BCDR carve-out. 07_bcdr.md cl. 5.1, 5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.3, 9.1–9.3

BCDR permits up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on failback without the 5 Business Days' maintenance-window notice the SLA requires, and such downtime would exceed the 99.9% monthly allowance (c. 43 minutes) unless the disputed exclusion applies. 07_bcdr.md cl. 5.2 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.1, 3.4

Response and Resolution clocks start when Provider 'acknowledges the Incident in its service management tool', making the response target self-fulfilling and allowing Provider to defer the start of all targets indefinitely. 04_sla.md cl. 5.4

Priority 2/3 targets expressed in Business Days are incoherent with the support window: support is only 08:00–18:00 on Business Days, so a 'Resolution within one Business Day' target is ambiguous as to whether out-of-hours time counts, and the disputed Business Day definition compounds this. 04_sla.md cl. 2.2, 5.2–5.3 vs cl. 1.1

The DPA's 'PRECEDENCE' clause contains no precedence rule at all — it merely states the Addendum forms part of the Agreement — leaving the DPA subordinate to the MSA and hence its data-protection controls overridden. 03_dpa.md cl. 12.1

Fines indemnity is circular/ambiguous: 'each party shall indemnify the other against fines imposed on it as a result of the other's breach' leaves 'it' undefined and, read literally, requires each party to indemnify the other for fines caused by the indemnifying party's own... or the other's breach — the clause is unworkable. 03_dpa.md cl. 11.2

Purchase-order gate conflicts with payment obligations: invoices without a valid PO number 'may be returned unpaid', which cuts across the MSA/SOW obligation to pay each undisputed invoice within a fixed period and provides no mechanism if the PO expires or is exhausted. 05_order_form.md cl. 5.1–5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.3
Order Form fixes a fixed Annual Contract Value while the MSA permits annual CPI-linked Fee increases, with no statement of which prevails on price. 05_order_form.md cl. 1.4, 1.7 vs 01_msa.md cl. 4.4

Deemed approval of Change Requests by Customer silence coexists with Provider's right to price and implement changes, and no dispute mechanism preserves Customer's position once the 10-Business-Day clock lapses — a significant one-sided gap relative to MSA cl. 2.4. 08_change_control.md cl. 4.2, 4.4

Exit assistance is conditioned on Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which allows Provider to block mandatory transition assistance by pricing, and it applies even where termination is for Provider's breach. 09_exit.md cl. 1.2, 3.2, 3.4

Remediation timescales inconsistent within the security regime: critical penetration-test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for a critical finding that is also a patch. 06_infosec.md cl. 7.4 vs cl. 9.1

Duplicate and inconsistent post-incident reporting obligations: root cause analysis within 5 Business Days of Resolution under the SLA versus a written incident report within 10 Business Days of closing the incident under the Information Security Policy, for the same incident. 04_sla.md cl. 8.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl. 6.2

Governance overlap without reconciliation: incident/change reviews are assigned to a 'monthly service review' (SOW/SLA/Change Control) and to a 'quarterly security review' (Information Security Policy) that is not established in any document. 06_infosec.md cl. 6.3 vs 02_sow.md cl. 8.1

Assumption without consequence: the SOW assumes no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters but specifies no relief, charge or change mechanism if that assumption fails. 02_sow.md cl. 10.3

Document set is mislabelled and incomplete as described: documents 1–4 are headed 'DOCUMENT n of 4' but the set contains nine documents (Order Form, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure and Exit Plan are unnumbered additions), and the MSA's structure clause designates only Schedule 1. Headers of 01_msa.md–04_sla.md vs 05–09; 01_msa.md cl. 2.1

Documents 4 and 6–9 style themselves Schedules 2–6 to the MSA, but the MSA requires a Schedule to be 'executed by both parties and expressly stated to be a Schedule'; none bears execution provisions (only the Order Form is signed), so their status as part of the Agreement is doubtful. 04_sla.md, 06_infosec.md, 07_bcdr.md, 08_change_control.md, 09_exit.md headers vs 01_msa.md cl. 1.6

Order Form 'Named support contact: Provider's service desk' and the DPA/SLA references to a 'nominated security contact' and 'nominated technical contact' are undefined or unpopulated — no security contact is named anywhere and the referenced contact annex does not exist. 05_order_form.md cl. 3.2, 4 vs 04_sla.md cl. 7.3–7.4 and 07_bcdr.md cl. 4.2
Personnel-substitution clause refers to 'named key personnel' but no personnel are named in any document, making the restriction inoperable. 02_sow.md cl. 3.5

Availability measurement bases differ: the SOW measures across each calendar month excluding agreed maintenance windows, the SLA uses a total-minutes formula with maintenance and further exclusions, and the BCDR adds continuity exclusions — producing different results from the same outage. 02_sow.md cl. 7.3 vs 04_sla.md cl. 3.2–3.3, 9 vs 07_bcdr.md cl. 5.3

InfoSec Policy allows Customer data to be stored/processed in 'any Provider region' as determined by Provider's CISO, with only 30 days' after-the-fact notice — directly contrary to the DPA's UK/EEA restriction, approved-location annex, and prior-authorisation requirement. 06_infosec.md cl.2.1/2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1–4.3

BCDR recovery site in Frankfurt, Germany is not among the DPA's approved processing locations (London, Dublin), so invoking the recovery site breaches the DPA. 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1 vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2/cl.4.3

Encryption scope conflict: DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while the InfoSec Policy requires encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data', leaving Internal Data (which includes personal data such as contact details and transaction records) unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.3.1/1.3

Data retention obligations are mutually impossible: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days then deletion; InfoSec requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months. 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3/5.2; 06_infosec.md cl.5.2

Exit deliverables cannot be met alongside deletion timetables: Provider must hand over all Customer data at the end of a transition period ending 6 months after termination, yet must delete Customer Personal Data within 30 days (DPA) and delete remaining data after 90 days (Exit cl.2.3). 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.2 and 09_exit.md cl.2.3

Data return format conflict: DPA requires return in a 'structured, commonly used format'; Exit Plan requires return 'in the format used by Provider's systems'. 03_dpa.md cl.8.1 vs 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a)

Internal contradiction in Exit Plan retention/deletion: cl.2.3 fixes retention at 90 days post-termination, while cl.5.2 defers deletion until after both that period and completion of handover, which may occur up to 6 months post-termination. 09_exit.md cl.2.3 vs cl.5.2

Confidentiality definitions conflict: MSA limits Confidential Information to material marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; MSA precedence would strip DPA protection. 01_msa.md cl.11.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination while records/data containing that information must be retained for 7 years, leaving 4 years of unprotected retained data. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4

DPA governing law is internally contradictory and conflicts with the MSA: cl.13.1 adopts the law of the Agreement (England and Wales) 'save as provided in cl.13.2', and cl.13.2 then imposes the laws of the Republic of Ireland, while the MSA gives English courts exclusive jurisdiction. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1–13.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.15.1–15.2

Change control conflict: MSA requires every change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, whereas the Change Control Procedure permits deemed approval on Customer silence, unilateral Delivery Lead approval up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 01_msa.md cl.2.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Charge-increase controls conflict: MSA permits fee increases only once per 12 months on 60 days' notice and capped at CPI, while the Change Control Procedure exempts change-related charges from those notice requirements and lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve up to £35,000 of cost impact. 01_msa.md cl.4.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl.5.3, 4.3

Internal timing contradiction: a Change Request is deemed approved if Customer does not respond within 10 Business Days, yet escalation of a disagreement allows 5 Business Days per level across three levels (up to 15 Business Days) and expressly does not suspend the timetable — a disputed change can be deemed approved mid-escalation. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2 vs cl.8.1–8.3

Response/Resolution clock is circular and unmeasurable: times run from the moment Provider 'acknowledges the Incident in its service management tool', so the 15-minute response target is self-satisfying and Provider controls the start of its own deadlines. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 with cl.5.1–5.3
BCDR RTO of 8 hours is incompatible with the SLA Priority 1 Resolution target of 4 hours for the same total loss of platform availability. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.5.1

BCDR unilaterally suspends all Service Level Schedule obligations for the duration of a Continuity Event and excludes related downtime (including up to 12 hours' planned unavailability for failback) from availability, gutting the 99.9% commitment with no cap or Customer consent — and conflicting with MSA precedence over Schedules. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1–5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1/3.3

The Order Form is neither a Schedule nor an Addendum as defined in the MSA (Agreement = MSA plus Schedules and Addenda executed under it), so a document outside the defined Agreement claims the highest precedence over it. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1–2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.1/1.6

The Order Form's precedence list ranks Schedules above Addenda, meaning the SLA's weaker 72-hour, narrowly defined security incident regime overrides the DPA's 24-hour regime and the DPA's unlimited-liability provision — an outcome inconsistent with the DPA's own terms. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1(c)–(d) vs 03_dpa.md cl.6.1/11.1

Purchase order condition allows invoices without a PO number to be 'returned unpaid', overriding the MSA payment obligation with no mechanism for PO expiry/exhaustion or restart of payment terms. 05_order_form.md cl.5.1–5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3

Log retention (18 months, then mandatory deletion) conflicts with the MSA obligation to retain all records for 7 years and with the ability to evidence historic incidents in audits. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4/10.1

Record retention for the SLA reports and the change log is limited to 'the duration of the Agreement', contradicting the MSA's 7-year post-termination retention obligation and the Exit Plan requirement to hand over the change log at exit. 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 09_exit.md cl.4.1(e)

Remediation timescales inconsistent: critical penetration-test findings must be fixed within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for a critical finding that is also a patchable vulnerability. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

InfoSec 'Restricted Data' includes payment card data, but the DPA's stated categories of personal data exclude payment card data, so the documents disagree on what data is in scope of the Services. 06_infosec.md cl.1.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.3.3/Annex 1

Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services for up to 6 months after the effective date of termination, but no charging basis, fee, or contractual continuation mechanism is provided and the MSA/Order Form terms have by then expired ('on the terms then in force' is indeterminate). 09_exit.md cl.2.1–2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.3, 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Exit obligations are conditioned on Customer approving a cost estimate before assistance begins, which can block the mandatory milestones (e.g. exit plan confirmed at T+15 Business Days) and contradicts the unconditional assistance duty. 09_exit.md cl.3.4 vs cl.3.1 and Annex 1 milestones

Exit knowledge transfer requires the Delivery Lead and a solution architect for up to 6 months post-termination, but the SOW team commitment and key-person obligations end with the SOW, with no resourcing obligation surviving termination. 09_exit.md cl.6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.1–3.5

DPA mutual indemnity for regulatory fines conflicts with the MSA liability cap that expressly applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, leaving it unclear whether the indemnity is capped. 03_dpa.md cl.11.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.1/13.3

DPA 'Precedence' section is a heading with no precedence rule — it states only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement, leaving DPA/MSA conflicts unresolved and defaulting to the MSA prevailing over data protection terms. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

Document set is internally miscounted: the instructions and document headers state 'DOCUMENT 1 of 4' through '4 of 4', but nine documents (including Schedules 3–6 and an Order Form) are in fact included and cross-referenced. All documents — cover headers (01–09)

SOW assumption that no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters carries no stated consequence or link to the Change Control Procedure if the assumption fails, leaving scope and cost undetermined. 02_sow.md cl.10.3

'Data Protection Law' is defined by reference to the territories where the Services are provided, which is itself contested between documents (UK/EEA per DPA, India per SOW, any region per InfoSec), making the applicable law indeterminate. 03_dpa.md cl.1.2 with 02_sow.md cl.3.4, 06_infosec.md cl.2.1

Internally self-defeating records provision: MSA requires Provider to make records available on reasonable request 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes all inspection/audit rights. 01_msa.md cl.12.2 with cl.10.2

findings: Circular order of precedence: MSA 14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, SOW 1.2 says the SOW (Schedule 1) prevails over the MSA, and Order Form 2.1/2.2 says the Order Form prevails over everything while ranking the MSA above Schedules. No conflict can be resolved deterministically. 01_msa.md cl.14.2; 02_sow.md cl.1.2; 05_order_form.md cl.2.1-2.2

The Order Form claims top precedence but is not a 'Schedule' or 'Addendum' as defined in MSA 1.1/1.6, so on the MSA's own terms it arguably does not form part of the Agreement at all; its precedence clause has no anchor in the MSA. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6; 05_order_form.md cl.2
Monthly Fee stated inconsistently: £12,400 in the MSA versus £12,800 in the SOW for the same Services. 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1
Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 x £12,800 (the SOW figure) and is irreconcilable with the MSA's £12,400/month (£148,800/year). 05_order_form.md cl.1.4 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.1

Three incompatible payment terms for the same invoices: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Initial term conflict: MSA initial term is 24 months, the Order Form initial term is 12 months, and the SOW programme runs 36 months. The 36-month programme cannot be completed within either stated term without guaranteed renewal. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2; 02_sow.md cl.2.1

Renewal/termination notice conflict: MSA allows termination for convenience on 90 days' notice and renews for 12-month periods after a 24-month term; the Order Form requires only 30 days' notice of non-renewal of a 12-month term; the SOW allows termination on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md cl.3.2-3.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.1-6.2; 02_sow.md cl.2.3

Commencement dates conflict: the MSA is effective 1 April 2027 and the Order Form Service Commencement Date is 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027 — one month before the agreement under which it is issued exists, and before the 12 March 2027 signature date. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md cl.2.2; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3, 7.3
Availability target stated twice at different levels for the same platform: 99.5% in the SOW and 99.9% in the SLA Schedule. 02_sow.md cl.7.2; 04_sla.md cl.3.1
Service credit cap conflict: SOW allows credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee; SLA caps credits at 10% of the monthly Fee for the same month. 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures in the SLA, which conflicts with the SOW's free-standing credit entitlement and with the general damages/liability regime in the MSA. 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.13.1
Automatic application of service credits to the next invoice is a deduction/set-off, which the MSA expressly prohibits absent Provider's written agreement. 04_sla.md cl.4.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.5
'Monthly Fee' used as the base for service credits is ambiguous because two different monthly Fees are defined (£12,400 / £12,800). 04_sla.md cl.4.2; 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.1.4, 4.1

Service level start date conflict: SOW says service levels begin at the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme); the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027), when no platform yet exists — an impossible obligation. 02_sow.md cl.7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.3; 04_sla.md cl.3.1
Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; SLA provides P2/P3 support only 08:00-18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl.3.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.2.2

'Business Day' defined two incompatible ways: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA), in a contract governed by English law. All Business-Day-based deadlines are therefore indeterminate. 01_msa.md cl.1.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.1.1

'Security Incident' defined two incompatible ways: broadly in the DPA (any unauthorised access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction) versus narrowly in the SLA (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption). The SLA definition excludes most DPA-notifiable events. 03_dpa.md cl.1.6 vs 04_sla.md cl.7.1
Three irreconcilable security incident notification deadlines: 24 hours (DPA), 72 hours (SLA), 48 hours (Information Security Policy). 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 04_sla.md cl.7.3; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1

Reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to 'Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum' for security escalation contacts; the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4 vs 03_dpa.md Annexes
Reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan points to 'Data Processing Addendum, clause 14'; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3

Reference to a non-existent clause and body: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to 'the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17'; the MSA ends at clause 16 and defines no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1

Reference to non-existent acceptance criteria: the MSA requires assessment against criteria in 'Schedule 1, Section 12'; the SOW (Schedule 1) has only 10 sections and contains no acceptance criteria at all, leaving the acceptance and warranty regime inoperable. 01_msa.md cl.6.2, 8.2 vs 02_sow.md

Acceptance mechanism directly contradictory: the MSA states no Deliverable is accepted unless expressly confirmed in writing, while the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. 01_msa.md cl.6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.3

Deliverables are not identified anywhere binding: the MSA defines 'Deliverable' as an item identified in a Statement of Work, but the SOW defers the list to a 'phase plan maintained by the delivery lead' — a document unilaterally controlled by Provider and outside the contract. 01_msa.md cl.1.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.1

Audit rights contradictory: the MSA states that after delivery of the SOC 2 report Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider premises or systems; the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1-9.2

Internally self-defeating provision: MSA 12.2 requires Provider to make records available to Customer 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 abolishes any right of inspection — the obligation cancels itself. 01_msa.md cl.12.2 and 10.2

Subcontracting conflict: the MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior specific written consent. Because the MSA prevails (cl.14.2), the DPA's subprocessor control is nullified. 01_msa.md cl.9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.5.1

Liability caps conflict three ways: MSA cap of 12 months' Fees stated to apply notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum; SOW cap of £250,000; DPA stating that no limitation in the Agreement applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md cl.9.2; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1
Insurance limits conflict: professional indemnity of not less than £5,000,000 in the MSA versus not less than £2,000,000 in the SOW for the same Services. 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Governing law conflict: the MSA is governed by the laws of England and Wales with exclusive English jurisdiction, while the DPA states it is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md cl.15.1-15.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.13.2

Internally circular/self-cancelling governing law clause: DPA 13.1 adopts the Agreement's law 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and 13.2 then displaces it entirely, so 13.1 has no content. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1-13.2

Clause headed 'Precedence' contains no precedence rule, leaving the DPA's status relative to the MSA, SOW and other Schedules undetermined (and subordinate under MSA 14.2, defeating its data protection protections). 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

'Confidential Information' defined two ways: the MSA requires written marking at disclosure; the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked. Under MSA 14.2 the marking requirement prevails, stripping protection from unmarked personal data. 01_msa.md cl.11.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality expires 3 years after termination while Provider must retain records and data for 7 years and personal data must be treated as confidential indefinitely — retained data would sit unprotected for 4 years. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Retention/deletion obligations cannot all be satisfied: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days then deletion. 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3, 5.2

Log retention conflict: security logs must be retained 18 months 'and then deleted', which conflicts with the MSA's 7-year record retention obligation and with the DPA's evidential/audit requirements. 06_infosec.md cl.5.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Record retention 'for the duration of the Agreement' for service reports and the change log conflicts with the MSA's 7-year post-termination retention obligation and with the exit obligation to hand over the change log. 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 09_exit.md cl.4.1(e)

Data location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and requires prior written authorisation for any transfer, while the Information Security Policy lets Provider store and process Customer data in any Provider region as determined by Provider's own CISO, with mere 30 days' after-the-fact notice of new regions. 03_dpa.md cl.4.1-4.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 2.3

The delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, which necessarily involves access to (and therefore transfer of) Customer Personal Data outside the UK/EEA, contrary to the DPA's location restriction and its list of approved locations. 02_sow.md cl.3.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.1, Annex 2

Disaster recovery site conflict: the BCDR Plan uses Frankfurt, Germany as the secondary recovery environment, but the DPA's approved locations annex lists only London (primary) and Dublin (disaster recovery). Frankfurt is unapproved and Dublin is unused. 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1 vs 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Encryption scope conflict: the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while the Information Security Policy requires encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data', leaving personal data classified as Internal Data unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.3.1, 1.3

Data category mismatch: the Information Security Policy contemplates payment card data and employee compensation data, neither of which appears in the DPA's exhaustive categories of personal data (contact details, transaction records, loyalty identifiers) or Annex 1. 06_infosec.md cl.1.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.3.3, Annex 1

RTO of 8 hours is inconsistent with the Priority 1 Resolution target of 4 hours, and a Security Incident/Continuity Event is deemed Priority 1 — the same outage carries two conflicting restoration deadlines. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.5.1, 7.2

Availability exclusions inconsistent: the SLA excludes only agreed maintenance windows (and the cl.9 exclusions), while the BCDR Plan additionally excludes all continuity-event and fail-back unavailability — including up to 12 hours of planned unavailability that is not an 'agreed maintenance window' and is not given the required 5 Business Days' notice. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2-5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.3, 3.4, 9

Blanket suspension of all Service Level Schedule obligations during a Continuity Event has no time limit or cap and conflicts with the SLA's availability and credit regime, which contains no such suspension. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1, 4.1

Measuring both response and resolution times from Provider's own acknowledgement in its service management tool makes the response targets circular (response time is always zero) and lets Provider control the start of the clock; it also conflicts with the definition of Incident occurrence. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 and 5.1-5.3

Priority 2 Resolution 'within one Business Day' is unworkable against support hours of 08:00-18:00 on Business Days combined with an undefined/conflicting Business Day definition; a P2 raised at 17:59 has effectively the same target as one raised at 08:00. 04_sla.md cl.5.2, 2.2, 1.1

Change control conflicts with the MSA requirement that any change to the Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation: the Procedure permits deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4

Escalation timetable is incoherent with deemed approval: three escalation levels at 5 Business Days each (up to 15 Business Days) exceed the 10 Business Day deemed-approval window, so a disputed change is deemed approved while the dispute is still being escalated; cl.8.3 expressly refuses to suspend the timetable. 08_change_control.md cl.8.1-8.3 vs cl.4.2

Cross-reference to a rate that does not exist: charges for preparing an impact assessment for a rejected Change Request are said to be 'at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan', which contains only a transition assistance day rate and no impact assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.3.2

Change-related charge increases are exempted from the notice requirements applying to ordinary increases, contradicting the MSA's single annual CPI-capped increase mechanism and the fixed Annual Contract Value in the Order Form. 08_change_control.md cl.5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.4; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4

Exit obligations are impossible to satisfy alongside data deletion: Provider must continue providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, yet must delete all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination and all Customer data after 90 days. 09_exit.md cl.2.1-2.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3

Exit data return format conflicts with the DPA: 'the format used by Provider's systems' versus a 'structured, commonly used format'; the DPA also gives a return right only 'during the term', leaving no return right at termination. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Double-charging conflict: transition assistance is chargeable at £1,250 per person per day and Provider must continue the Services 'on the terms then in force' (i.e. within the monthly Fee), while the SOW states the Fee covers all personnel. 09_exit.md cl.2.2, 3.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.5.2

Exit assistance is conditioned on Customer approving Provider's effort estimate before assistance begins, which allows Provider to stall the fixed Annex 1 milestones and the certified handover deadline. 09_exit.md cl.3.4 vs cl.7.1 and Annex 1

Named contacts inconsistent with the MSA requirement for a single Customer point of contact: the Order Form names separate commercial and technical Customer contacts, and other documents variously address a 'nominated contact', 'nominated security contact' and 'nominated technical contact' with no reconciliation. 05_order_form.md cl.4 vs 01_msa.md cl.5.2; 04_sla.md cl.7.3; 07_bcdr.md cl.4.2

Purchase order condition conflicts with the payment obligation: invoices lacking a PO number 'may be returned unpaid', whereas the MSA obliges Customer to pay each undisputed invoice within the stated period without deduction. 05_order_form.md cl.5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3, 4.5

Termination cure period of 15 days for material breach is inconsistent with the exit/transition machinery (transition period triggered by notice, six-month run-off) and with the SOW's separate 30-day convenience right; termination of the MSA would leave the 36-month SOW without a contractual framework. 01_msa.md cl.3.4 vs 09_exit.md cl.2.1; 02_sow.md cl.2.3-2.4

Document set is mislabelled and incomplete: the instructions and headers describe 'DOCUMENT 1 of 4' through 'DOCUMENT 4 of 4', but nine documents are supplied (Documents 5-9 bear no 'of' count), so the contractual set is not definitively identified anywhere. All documents — headers; 01_msa.md cl.1.1

Remediation timescales inconsistent: critical penetration test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for a critical finding remedied by a patch. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

Provider's unilateral right to determine security matters conflicts with the processor's duty to act only on Customer's documented instructions: the CISO decides data location and Restricted Data access, and Provider may change the Policy with mere notice of material changes. 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 4.2, 10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.2.2

Mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is unworkable/unenforceable as drafted and conflicts with the DPA's own disapplication of all liability limits, creating uncapped, potentially reciprocal exposure with no allocation mechanism. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1-11.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3

Provider must comply with Customer's reasonable instructions as to the manner of performance, yet the Change Control Procedure requires all scope/timetable changes to pass through formal change control and permits Provider-side unilateral approvals — the two mechanisms are not reconciled. 01_msa.md cl.2.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl.1.1, 4.3

BCDR test notice and reporting periods use Business Days while remediation and rehearsal reports use 'one (1) month', mixing incompatible time units across documents with two conflicting Business Day definitions. 07_bcdr.md cl.6.2-6.4; 09_exit.md cl.9.3

findings: Circular precedence: MSA clause 14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule, SOW section 1.2 says the SOW (Schedule 1) prevails over the MSA, and Order Form clause 2.2 says the Order Form prevails over any other document. The three precedence rules cannot be reconciled. 01_msa.md cl.14.2; 02_sow.md cl.1.2; 05_order_form.md cl.2.1-2.2

The Order Form purports to sit at the top of the precedence order, but it is neither a 'Schedule' (MSA 1.6: a document expressly stated to be a Schedule) nor an 'Addendum', so it falls outside the definition of 'Agreement' in MSA 1.1 and has no contractual status to confer precedence on itself. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6; 05_order_form.md cl.2

Monthly Fee stated three inconsistent ways: £12,400 in the MSA, £12,800 in the SOW, and an Annual Contract Value of £153,600 in the Order Form (which equals 12 x £12,800, not 12 x £12,400). 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4

Payment terms conflict three ways: 30 days from receipt (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from date of invoice (Order Form). The trigger event also differs (receipt vs invoice date). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Initial term conflict: MSA states 24 months, the Order Form states 12 months from the Service Commencement Date, and the SOW commits to a 36-month programme. The 36-month programme cannot be completed within either the 24-month or 12-month initial term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 02_sow.md cl.2.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Start date conflict: the MSA Effective Date and the Order Form Service Commencement Date are 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme is stated to commence on 1 March 2027 — one month before the agreement under which it is issued exists, and before the 12 March 2027 signature date on the Order Form. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md cl.2.2; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3, 7.3

Termination notice conflict: MSA requires 90 days' notice for termination for convenience, the SOW allows termination of the SOW on 30 days' notice, and the Order Form allows non-renewal on 30 days' notice. Terminating the SOW on 30 days' notice defeats the MSA's 90-day protection while leaving the MSA fee obligation in place. 01_msa.md cl.3.3; 02_sow.md cl.2.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.2
Availability target conflict: SOW requires not less than 99.5% monthly availability; the SLA requires not less than 99.9%. 02_sow.md cl.7.2; 04_sla.md cl.3.1
Service credit cap conflict: SOW allows credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee; the SLA caps credits at 10% of the monthly Fee for that month. 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 04_sla.md cl.4.2

Service level start date conflict: SOW says service levels apply only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme); the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md cl.7.1; 05_order_form.md cl.3.3

Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; the SLA restricts Priority 2 and Priority 3 support to 08:00-18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl.3.1; 04_sla.md cl.2.1-2.2

'Business Day' is defined twice and incompatibly: Monday to Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday to Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA). The US-holiday definition is also incoherent in an England and Wales-governed contract, and every deadline expressed in Business Days across the other Schedules is therefore ambiguous. 01_msa.md cl.1.2; 04_sla.md cl.1.1

'Security Incident' is defined twice and incompatibly: the DPA definition covers any unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction; the SLA definition is limited to confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of data. Many DPA incidents would not be an SLA Security Incident. 03_dpa.md cl.1.6; 04_sla.md cl.7.1

Confidentiality definition conflict: MSA 11.1 limits Confidential Information to material marked confidential at the time of disclosure, while DPA 1.4 deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked. Under the MSA precedence clause the narrower definition would prevail, leaving unmarked personal data unprotected. 01_msa.md cl.11.1; 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination, yet Provider must hold records and data for 7 years (MSA 12.4) — data held for four years with no confidentiality obligation attaching to it. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 and cl.12.4

Set-off conflict: the SLA requires Provider to apply service credits automatically to the next invoice, whereas MSA 4.5 requires Customer to pay all amounts without any set-off, deduction or withholding except as agreed by Provider in writing. 04_sla.md cl.4.1; 01_msa.md cl.4.5

The SLA makes service credits Customer's 'sole financial remedy' for availability failures, which conflicts with the SOW credit regime and with the general liability regime in MSA clause 13 (and with DPA 11.1 where an availability failure also breaches the Addendum). 04_sla.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.13

Circular/meaningless measurement: SLA response and Resolution times are measured from the point at which Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute 'response' target is self-satisfying and Provider controls the clock start rather than Customer's report time. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 with cl.5.1-5.3

The BCDR recovery objectives are inconsistent with the SLA availability commitment: 99.9% monthly availability permits roughly 43 minutes of downtime per month, whereas an 8-hour RTO plus up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on return equals about 20 hours. The BCDR Plan cures this only by unilaterally suspending SLA obligations and creating exclusions that the SLA's own exclusion list (agreed maintenance windows only) does not recognise. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.1-5.3; 04_sla.md cl.3.1, 3.3, 9.3

The BCDR return-to-primary unavailability is treated as excluded, but the SLA only excludes 'agreed maintenance windows' notified 5 Business Days in advance — impossible for an unplanned Continuity Event, so the exclusion cannot be satisfied on the SLA's terms. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2-5.3; 04_sla.md cl.3.4, 9.3

Change control escalation timetable conflicts with deemed approval: a Change Request is deemed approved if Customer does not respond within 10 Business Days, yet escalation gives each of three levels 5 Business Days (up to 15) and expressly does not suspend the timetable, so a change under active dispute can be deemed approved. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 8.1-8.3

Change-related charges are stated not to be subject to the notice requirements for charge increases, contradicting MSA 4.4 which allows only one increase in any 12-month period on 60 days' notice capped by CPI — a route to uncapped, un-noticed fee increases. 08_change_control.md cl.5.3; 01_msa.md cl.4.4

SOW phase durations (3 + 15 + 12 + 6 months = 36 months) fit the stated 36-month programme only if no phase overlaps, but the programme would then run to February 2030, beyond the MSA initial term ending 31 March 2029 and far beyond the Order Form's 12-month initial term, with no provision linking programme completion to renewal. 02_sow.md cl.2.1-2.2, 4.1-4.5; 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

MSA warranty that Deliverables 'will conform to the applicable acceptance criteria' is unenforceable because no acceptance criteria exist anywhere in the document set (the cross-referenced Schedule 1 Section 12 does not exist and the SOW defers deliverables to a Provider-maintained phase plan). 01_msa.md cl.8.2, 6.2; 02_sow.md cl.6.1

Mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is internally incoherent and conflicts with the liability regime: each party indemnifies the other for fines 'imposed on it as a result of the other's breach', while DPA 11.1 removes all caps, contradicting MSA 13.3's statement that the cap applies notwithstanding any Addendum. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1-11.2; 01_msa.md cl.13.3

The DPA states that 'Annex 1 sets out the processing details in full', but Annex 1 omits the nature of the processing, retention periods and technical measures, and describes 'hosting Services' that are not part of the SOW scope (replatforming programme). 03_dpa.md cl.3.4, Annex 1; 02_sow.md cl.2.1

DPA clause 12 is headed 'PRECEDENCE' but contains only a statement that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement — it establishes no precedence rule, leaving data protection terms subordinate to the MSA under MSA 14.2 despite DPA 11.1 purporting to override the MSA liability cap. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

The Order Form's PO requirement (invoices without a valid PO number may be returned unpaid) conflicts with the MSA obligation to pay each undisputed invoice within 30 days without deduction or withholding, and with the absence of any PO condition in the MSA or SOW. 05_order_form.md cl.5.2-5.3; 01_msa.md cl.4.3, 4.5

Renewal conflict: MSA renews for successive 12-month periods unless terminated on 90 days' notice under clause 3.3, while the Order Form renews for 12-month periods unless notice of non-renewal is given 30 days before term end; the two renewal clocks also run from different dates (MSA Effective Date term of 24 months vs Order Form 12-month term). 01_msa.md cl.3.2-3.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.1-6.2

Exit deadlock: Provider need not begin transition assistance until Customer approves an estimate that Provider has up to 15 Business Days to produce, yet Annex 1 requires the exit plan to be confirmed with the incoming supplier by T+15 Business Days and the data extract by T+30 Business Days. 09_exit.md cl.3.3-3.4, Annex 1 milestones 1-2

Exit Plan Annex 1 measures milestones from T = effective date of termination, but the transition period is defined as beginning on the date notice is given (up to 90 days earlier under MSA 3.3), leaving the first part of the transition period unmilestoned and the milestone baseline inconsistent with clause 2.1. 09_exit.md cl.2.1 and Annex 1

Exit Plan requires delivery of source code and all Deliverables at exit, but MSA 7.2 assigns Deliverable IP only on payment in full and MSA 7.3 reserves Provider's pre-existing tools and methods, so on termination for Provider breach or non-payment dispute the handover obligation and the IP position conflict. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(b); 01_msa.md cl.7.2-7.3

The Exit Plan requires a Delivery Lead and solution architect to be available during the transition period and the SOW requires an 11-FTE team, but the SOW also prohibits substitution of key personnel without Customer consent, with no mechanism for staffing after SOW termination while the MSA transition obligations continue. 09_exit.md cl.6.1; 02_sow.md cl.3.1, 3.5, 2.3

InfoSec remediation timescales are inconsistent: critical penetration test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no rule for a critical finding that is remedied by a patch. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 and cl.9.1

Document set numbering is defective: the headers run 'DOCUMENT 1 of 4' to 'DOCUMENT 4 of 4' but five further documents (5 to 9) are included in the same set, so the stated composition of the contract set is wrong and it is unclear which documents were intended to form the agreement. All documents — headers (01_msa.md through 09_exit.md)

Schedules 2 to 6 (SLA, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure, Exit Plan) are described as Schedules to the MSA, but the MSA only designates Schedule 1 and defines a Schedule as a document executed by both parties; none of these documents carries an execution block, so their status within the 'Agreement' is uncertain. 01_msa.md cl.1.6, 2.1; 04_sla.md, 06_infosec.md, 07_bcdr.md, 08_change_control.md, 09_exit.md headers

SOW section 9.3 excludes liability for indirect and consequential loss and 9.2 caps Provider liability only, whereas the MSA liability regime is mutual and contains no such exclusion; the Schedules therefore alter the MSA's risk allocation in a manner MSA 13.3 forbids. 02_sow.md cl.9.2-9.3; 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3

SOW assumption that no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters has no stated consequence or remedy if it proves wrong, and no link to the Change Control Procedure, leaving scope and price open-ended. 02_sow.md cl.10.3

BCDR Invocation may be declared only by Provider's Head of Operations, giving Customer no right to invoke and no alternate authoriser if that individual is unavailable, while the SLA's Priority 1 obligations are simultaneously suspended by Invocation — Provider controls both the trigger and its own relief. 07_bcdr.md cl.4.1, 5.1
