findings: Set is internally mislabelled: each of the first four files is headed "DOCUMENT n of 4" but the contract set actually contains nine documents (Order Form, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure, Exit Plan are all additional). The instruction to review "four documents" cannot be reconciled with the nine supplied. Headers of 01_msa.md, 02_sow.md, 03_dpa.md, 04_sla.md vs documents 05–09

Circular order of precedence: MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum; SOW (Schedule 1) says the SOW prevails over the MSA; the Order Form says it prevails over every other document even though it is neither a Schedule nor an Addendum. No conflict can be resolved. MSA cl. 14.2; SOW cl. 1.2; Order Form cl. 2.1–2.2

The Order Form is not within the defined "Agreement": MSA cl. 1.1 defines the Agreement as the MSA plus Schedules and Addenda, and cl. 1.6 defines Schedule narrowly. The Order Form is described as neither, so its claimed top-ranking precedence has no contractual hook. MSA cl. 1.1, 1.6 vs Order Form cl. 2.1

Precedence ranking does not order Schedules among themselves (SOW, SLA, InfoSec, BCDR, Change Control, Exit are all "any Schedule"), so the many Schedule-versus-Schedule conflicts (e.g. availability, credits, notification times) are unresolvable. Order Form cl. 2.1(c); MSA cl. 14.2
Monthly Fee stated in two different amounts: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW for the same Services. MSA cl. 4.1 vs SOW cl. 5.1
Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800 (the SOW figure) and contradicts the MSA figure (12 × £12,400 = £148,800). Order Form cl. 1.4 vs MSA cl. 4.1
Three incompatible payment terms for the same invoices: 30 days from receipt, 45 days from receipt, and 60 days from invoice date. MSA cl. 4.3 vs SOW cl. 5.3 vs Order Form cl. 1.6

Three incompatible term lengths: MSA initial term 24 months; Order Form initial term 12 months; SOW programme duration 36 months. The 36-month programme cannot be delivered within either shorter term. MSA cl. 3.1 vs Order Form cl. 1.2 vs SOW cl. 2.1

Start-date conflict: the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027, a month before the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027) and the Order Form Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) — i.e. work begins before the contract exists. SOW cl. 2.2 vs MSA Effective Date; Order Form cl. 1.3
The Order Form is dated 12 March 2027, after the SOW programme start date of 1 March 2027. Order Form cl. 7.3 vs SOW cl. 2.2

Termination/non-renewal notice periods conflict: 90 days for convenience under the MSA, 30 days for the SOW, and 30 days for Order Form non-renewal of the same commercial arrangement. MSA cl. 3.3 vs SOW cl. 2.3 vs Order Form cl. 6.2
Availability target stated at two levels for the same platform: 99.5% in the SOW and 99.9% in the SLA. SOW cl. 7.2 vs SLA cl. 3.1

Service credit cap conflict: up to 25% of the monthly Fee in the SOW versus a maximum of 10% in the SLA; also creates potential double recovery for one availability failure. SOW cl. 7.4 vs SLA cl. 4.2

Service levels commencement conflict: SOW says service levels start at the beginning of Phase 3 (approximately month 19), the Order Form says they apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). SOW cl. 7.1 vs Order Form cl. 3.3
Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; SLA limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. Order Form cl. 3.1 vs SLA cl. 2.2

"Business Day" is defined twice and inconsistently: Monday–Friday excluding England & Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA). Every SLA deadline is therefore ambiguous, and the US-holiday calendar is incoherent with English governing law and an India-based team. MSA cl. 1.2 vs SLA cl. 1.1

"Security Incident" is defined twice and inconsistently: the DPA definition is broad (any unauthorised access, alteration, loss, etc.), the SLA definition is narrow (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption). The same event may or may not be an incident depending on document. DPA cl. 1.6 vs SLA cl. 7.1
Three incompatible security-incident notification deadlines for the same event: 24 hours (DPA), 72 hours (SLA), 48 hours (InfoSec Policy). DPA cl. 6.1 vs SLA cl. 7.3 vs InfoSec cl. 6.1

Cross-reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to "Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum" for security escalation contacts, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. SLA cl. 7.4 vs DPA Annexes

Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to "the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17", but the MSA ends at clause 16 and creates no Change Control Board. Change Control cl. 4.1 vs MSA (cl. 1–16)
Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan refers to "the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14", but the DPA ends at clause 13. Exit cl. 5.3 vs DPA cl. 13

Cross-reference to a non-existent provision: the MSA requires assessment against acceptance criteria "set out in Schedule 1, Section 12", but the SOW (Schedule 1) has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria. MSA cl. 6.2 vs SOW

The Provider warranty is measured against "the applicable acceptance criteria", but no acceptance criteria exist anywhere in the set (SOW leaves Deliverables to an uncontracted phase plan maintained by the Provider's delivery lead). MSA cl. 8.2; SOW cl. 6.1

Change Control refers to a charging rate for impact assessments "set out in the Exit and Transition Plan", but the Exit Plan contains only a transition-assistance day rate (£1,250) and no impact-assessment rate. Change Control cl. 7.2 vs Exit cl. 3.2

Acceptance mechanism conflict: MSA prohibits deemed acceptance and requires express written acceptance; SOW deems a Deliverable accepted if Customer is silent for five Business Days. MSA cl. 6.1 vs SOW cl. 6.3

Change approval conflict: MSA requires every change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval on Customer silence, unilateral Provider approval up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. MSA cl. 2.4 vs Change Control cl. 4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Internal inconsistency in Change Control: cl. 4.1 sends every impact-assessed Change Request to a Change Control Board, yet cl. 4.3 lets the Provider's Delivery Lead approve changes up to £35,000 without reference to Customer, and cl. 4.2 deems approval without any Board decision. Change Control cl. 4.1–4.3

Change Control cl. 5.3 disapplies the notice requirements for charge increases, contradicting the MSA's controls on Fee increases (once per 12 months, 60 days' notice, CPI cap), which the MSA says prevail. Change Control cl. 5.3 vs MSA cl. 4.4

Wrong internal cross-reference: escalation "does not suspend the timetable in clause 3", but the timetable in issue at the escalation stage is the approval timetable in clause 4, not the impact-assessment timetable in clause 3. Change Control cl. 8.3

Audit rights are simultaneously granted and excluded: the MSA states Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems; MSA precedence would strip the DPA right (and the statutory audit right a processor must give). MSA cl. 10.2 vs DPA cl. 9.1–9.2
MSA cl. 12.2 makes record access subject to cl. 10.2, which denies any audit/inspection right — so the record-availability obligation is self-cancelling. MSA cl. 12.1–12.2 with cl. 10.2

Retention versus deletion conflict that cannot be satisfied: MSA requires all records, data and materials to be retained for 7 years after termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires 90 days' retention then deletion. MSA cl. 12.4 vs DPA cl. 8.2 vs Exit cl. 2.3, 5.2

Log/report retention conflicts with the 7-year record retention obligation: security logs must be deleted after 18 months and service reports need only be kept for the duration of the Agreement. InfoSec cl. 5.2 and SLA cl. 6.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4
Confidentiality survival (3 years) is shorter than the mandatory 7-year retention of the same data, leaving retained Customer data unprotected for four years. MSA cl. 11.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees (~£148,800–£153,600) and states this applies notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SOW sets a £250,000 cap. MSA cl. 13.1, 13.3 vs SOW cl. 9.2

The DPA disapplies every limitation and exclusion of liability for any breach of the DPA or Data Protection Law, directly contradicting the MSA's overriding cap and the SOW's cap and consequential-loss exclusion; MSA precedence would in turn defeat the DPA provision. DPA cl. 11.1 vs MSA cl. 13.1/13.3 and SOW cl. 9.2–9.3
Insurance limit stated twice and inconsistently: professional indemnity of not less than £5,000,000 in the MSA versus not less than £2,000,000 in the SOW. MSA cl. 16.1 vs SOW cl. 9.4

Subcontracting conflict: the MSA permits subcontracting of any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA forbids engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. MSA cl. 9.3 vs DPA cl. 5.1

Governing law is contradictory: the MSA (which is stated to prevail) applies English law with exclusive English jurisdiction, while the DPA states it is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement "save as provided in clause 13.2" and then applies Irish law — an internal contradiction within the DPA and a conflict with the MSA. DPA cl. 13.1–13.2 vs MSA cl. 15.1–15.2

Data location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA with Annex 2 approving only London and Dublin, but the SOW places the delivery team (with system access) in Bengaluru, India. DPA cl. 4.1, Annex 2 vs SOW cl. 3.4

The InfoSec Policy allows Customer data to be stored and processed in any Provider region as determined by the Provider's CISO, with notification only 30 days after a new region enters service — irreconcilable with the DPA's UK/EEA restriction and prior-authorisation requirement. InfoSec cl. 2.1, 2.3 vs DPA cl. 4.1–4.2

Disaster recovery site conflict: the DPA's approved locations list Dublin as the disaster recovery site, while the BCDR Plan operates the secondary recovery environment in Frankfurt, Germany (a location not authorised under DPA cl. 4.2/Annex 2). DPA Annex 2 vs BCDR cl. 3.1

Encryption-at-rest scope conflict: the DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while the InfoSec Policy requires encryption at rest only for "Restricted Data", leaving most personal data (Internal Data) unencrypted. DPA cl. 7.2 vs InfoSec cl. 1.2–1.3, 3.1

Provider-controlled decision-making conflicts with processor status: the Provider's CISO unilaterally determines processing regions and access approvals, whereas the DPA requires processing only on Customer's documented instructions. InfoSec cl. 2.1, 4.2 vs DPA cl. 2.2

Confidentiality definitions conflict: the MSA restricts Confidential Information to material marked confidential at disclosure, while the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; MSA precedence would defeat the DPA provision. MSA cl. 11.1 vs DPA cl. 1.4

Post-incident reporting deadlines conflict for the same event (a Security Incident is a Priority 1 Incident): root cause analysis within 5 Business Days of Resolution versus written incident report within 10 Business Days of incident closure. SLA cl. 8.1 vs InfoSec cl. 6.2

Internally inconsistent SLA treatment of Security Incidents: they are treated as Priority 1 requiring resolution within 4 hours, yet notification to Customer need only occur within 72 hours of confirmation. SLA cl. 7.2 vs cl. 7.3

Response and Resolution clocks run from the point at which the Provider itself acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, making the 15-minute response target self-fulfilling and unmeasurable against Customer's report time. SLA cl. 5.4 with cl. 5.1–5.3
Automatic application of service credits to the next invoice conflicts with the MSA's prohibition on any set-off, deduction or withholding of amounts due. SLA cl. 4.1 vs MSA cl. 4.5

"Sole financial remedy" for availability failures conflicts with the SOW's separate credit entitlement and with the DPA's disapplication of all liability limits, and is not reconciled by any precedence rule between Schedules. SLA cl. 4.3 vs SOW cl. 7.4 and DPA cl. 11.1

BCDR suspends all Service Level Schedule obligations during a Continuity Event (including 24x7 Priority 1 support) and excludes up to 12 hours of return-to-primary unavailability from availability, but the SLA's exclusions list does not include Continuity Events; the two Schedules give different answers with no precedence rule. BCDR cl. 5.1–5.3 vs SLA cl. 2.1, 9.1–9.3

Recovery objectives are mathematically incompatible with the availability commitment: a 99.9% monthly target permits about 43 minutes of downtime, whereas the RTO alone is 8 hours plus up to 12 further hours of planned unavailability. BCDR cl. 2.1, 5.2 vs SLA cl. 3.1

A 24-hour Recovery Point Objective (up to 24 hours of data loss) is inconsistent with the DPA's duty to protect against loss of Customer Personal Data and with the 24-hour Security Incident notification regime treating loss as an incident. BCDR cl. 2.2 vs DPA cl. 1.6, 6.1, 7.1
Single-person dependency with no deputy: only the Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, so recovery cannot be invoked in that person's absence. BCDR cl. 4.1

Notification to "Customer's nominated security contact" is required, but no security contact is nominated anywhere in the set (the Order Form names only commercial, technical and delivery contacts; the MSA requires a single point of contact). SLA cl. 7.3 vs Order Form cl. 4 and MSA cl. 5.2

Contact-nomination conflict: the MSA requires a single point of contact for the Services, whereas the Order Form names separate commercial and technical contacts and other documents assume further nominated contacts. MSA cl. 5.2 vs Order Form cl. 4.1–4.2; BCDR cl. 4.2

Exit obligations extend beyond the life of the Agreement: the transition period ends six months after the effective date of termination and the Provider must keep providing the Services "on the terms then in force", although the Agreement (and the payment obligation) has ended and the DPA requires deletion of personal data within 30 days of termination. Exit cl. 2.1–2.2 vs MSA cl. 3 and DPA cl. 8.2
Data-return format conflict: the Exit Plan requires return "in the format used by Provider's systems", the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. Exit cl. 4.1(a) vs DPA cl. 8.1

Exit assistance is made conditional on Customer approving the Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which can defeat the unconditional obligation to assist on any termination (including termination for the Provider's breach). Exit cl. 3.4 vs cl. 1.2, 3.1

Charging ambiguity on exit: Services continue during transition "on the terms then in force" (monthly Fee) while transition assistance is separately chargeable at £1,250 per person per day, with no rule preventing double charging for the same personnel. Exit cl. 2.2 vs cl. 3.2

Exit milestone timings mix Business Days with the calendar transition period and can conflict: handover certification is due "end of transition period" (6 months) while earlier milestones run to T+90 Business Days, and no milestone is aligned to the 90-day data retention/deletion deadline in cl. 2.3. Exit Annex 1 vs Exit cl. 2.1, 2.3, 5.2

Unenforceable/vague indemnity: each party indemnifies the other against regulatory fines imposed on it, which is contrary to public policy in many cases and conflicts with the mutual disapplication of liability limits. DPA cl. 11.2 with cl. 11.1

The DPA's "Precedence" clause says only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement and resolves nothing, so the MSA's general precedence rule overrides the data protection terms it was intended to protect. DPA cl. 12.1 vs MSA cl. 14.2

Phase schedule leaves no room for the stated durations under the shorter contract terms and 4.5 permits overlap only by agreement, so the 3+15+12+6 = 36 month sequence cannot fit the 24-month MSA term or the 12-month Order Form term. SOW cl. 4.1–4.5 vs MSA cl. 3.1, Order Form cl. 1.2

Deliverables are defined by reference to a "phase plan maintained by the delivery lead" — a document unilaterally controlled by the Provider and not contractually fixed, which undermines the MSA definition of Deliverable, the acceptance regime and the IP assignment. SOW cl. 6.1 vs MSA cl. 1.3, 6, 7.2

Undefined term: the delivery lead must be available during "Customer's working hours", which is not defined anywhere and conflicts with the two competing Business Day definitions and the Bengaluru time zone. SOW cl. 3.3

Assumption with no consequence: the SOW assumes no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters, but no mechanism links a breach of that assumption to the Change Control Procedure or to relief. SOW cl. 10.3 vs Change Control Procedure

Purchase-order gating conflicts with the payment obligation: invoices without a valid PO may be returned unpaid, yet the MSA requires payment of undisputed invoices within 30 days and imposes no PO requirement. Order Form cl. 5.1–5.3 vs MSA cl. 4.3, 4.5

Renewal mechanics conflict: the MSA renews for 12-month periods terminable on 90 days' notice, while the Order Form renews for 12-month periods on 30 days' non-renewal notice, and neither addresses whether the SOW (36 months) or the Order Form controls the renewal of the same Services. MSA cl. 3.2–3.3 vs Order Form cl. 6.1–6.2 vs SOW cl. 2.1

The liability cap is expressed to apply to "each party's total aggregate liability", which would also cap Customer's obligation to pay the Fees, an unintended and inconsistent result given cl. 4.5. MSA cl. 13.1 vs cl. 4.1–4.5

Vague and unmeasurable obligations: exit rehearsal "at least once in the term" with no date, and reports due "within one (1) month" while comparable deadlines elsewhere are in Business Days. Exit cl. 9.2–9.3; BCDR cl. 6.4

Acknowledgement duty is one-sided/incoherent: either party may raise a Change Request, but only the Provider is obliged to acknowledge one, leaving Provider-raised requests with no acknowledgement trigger for the 10-Business-Day impact assessment. Change Control cl. 2.1, 2.3, 3.1

Remediation timelines for the same vulnerability class differ: critical penetration-test findings within 30 days but critical security patches within 14 days, with no rule on which applies. InfoSec cl. 7.4 vs cl. 9.1

Personnel screening and access commitments in the InfoSec Policy (criminal-record checks, MFA, quarterly reviews) apply to a Bengaluru delivery centre that the DPA's location restriction says should not hold Customer Personal Data at all — the two Schedules assume different operating models. InfoSec cl. 8.1, 4.3 vs DPA cl. 4.1 and SOW cl. 3.4

findings: Circular order of precedence: the MSA says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while Statement of Work 1 (a Schedule) says it prevails over the MSA, and the Order Form says it prevails over everything. No conflict between these three documents can be resolved. MSA cl. 14.2; SOW 1 cl. 1.2; Order Form cl. 2.1–2.2

The Order Form claims top precedence but is not part of the 'Agreement' as defined: MSA 1.1 defines the Agreement as the MSA plus Schedules and Addenda only, and MSA 1.6 requires a Schedule to be expressly stated to be a Schedule. The Order Form is neither, so it has no contractual status yet purports to override the MSA. MSA cl. 1.1, 1.6 vs Order Form cl. 2.1
Monthly Fee stated inconsistently: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in the SOW for the same Services. MSA cl. 4.1 vs SOW 1 cl. 5.1

Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals 12 × £12,800 and is inconsistent with the MSA fee of £12,400/month (£148,800 p.a.), so the Order Form silently contradicts the MSA figure it ranks below itself. Order Form cl. 1.4 vs MSA cl. 4.1
Three incompatible payment terms for the same invoices: 30 days from receipt, 45 days from receipt, and 60 days from invoice date. MSA cl. 4.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 5.3 vs Order Form cl. 1.6

Three incompatible term lengths: 24-month initial term (MSA), 36-month programme (SOW), 12-month initial term (Order Form). A 36-month programme cannot be performed within a 12- or 24-month term. MSA cl. 3.1 vs SOW 1 cl. 2.1 vs Order Form cl. 1.2

Programme start date (1 March 2027) precedes the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027), the Order Form Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027) and even the signature date (12 March 2027), creating obligations before the contract exists. SOW 1 cl. 2.2 vs MSA Effective Date; Order Form cl. 1.3, 7.3

Termination/renewal notice periods conflict: 90 days' notice for convenience termination under the MSA, 30 days for the SOW, and 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form. MSA cl. 3.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 2.3 vs Order Form cl. 6.2

'Business Day' defined two irreconcilable ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays. All SLA response/resolution and notice periods are therefore indeterminate (and the US-holiday definition is incongruous with English governing law and UK-based services). MSA cl. 1.2 vs SLA cl. 1.1
Availability target conflict: 99.5% monthly availability in the SOW versus 99.9% in the SLA for the same platform. SOW 1 cl. 7.2 vs SLA cl. 3.1
Service credit cap conflict: up to 25% of the monthly Fee in the SOW versus a maximum of 10% in the SLA. SOW 1 cl. 7.4 vs SLA cl. 4.2

Start of service levels conflicts: SOW applies service levels from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme), while the Order Form applies them from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). SOW 1 cl. 7.1 vs Order Form cl. 3.3
Support coverage conflict: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels; the SLA restricts Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. Order Form cl. 3.1 vs SLA cl. 2.2

Acceptance mechanism conflict: MSA prohibits deemed acceptance (express written acceptance required), while the SOW deems a Deliverable accepted after 5 Business Days' silence. MSA cl. 6.1 vs SOW 1 cl. 6.3

Cross-reference to a non-existent provision: acceptance criteria are said to be in 'Schedule 1, Section 12', but the SOW (Schedule 1) has only ten sections and contains no acceptance criteria at all. MSA cl. 6.2 vs SOW 1

The Deliverable warranty is measured against 'applicable acceptance criteria' that are never set out anywhere in the document set, making the warranty unenforceable/indeterminate. MSA cl. 8.2 (with SOW 1 s. 6)

Deliverables are defined in the MSA as items identified in a Statement of Work, but the SOW leaves them to a phase plan unilaterally maintained by Provider's delivery lead — the scope of the Deliverables is therefore undefined and controlled by one party. MSA cl. 1.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 6.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA states Customer has no right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems, while the DPA grants an annual audit including inspection of premises and systems (and the MSA prevails, gutting the DPA right and likely Data Protection Law compliance). MSA cl. 10.2 vs DPA cl. 9.1–9.2

Internal contradiction: Provider must make records available to Customer on reasonable request 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes any right of inspection. MSA cl. 12.2 with cl. 10.2

Irreconcilable data retention/deletion obligations: retain all records, data and materials for 7 years post-termination; delete all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; retain Customer data for 90 days post-termination then delete. These cannot all be performed. MSA cl. 12.4 vs DPA cl. 8.2 vs Exit Plan cl. 2.3 and 5.2
Security log retention of 18 months followed by deletion conflicts with the 7-year record retention obligation. InfoSec cl. 5.2 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Service report and change log retention limited to the duration of the Agreement conflicts with the 7-year post-termination retention obligation. SLA cl. 6.3 and Change Control cl. 9.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Governing law conflict and internal contradiction: the DPA says it is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement (England and Wales) 'save as provided in clause 13.2', and clause 13.2 then imposes the law of the Republic of Ireland; this also conflicts with the exclusive jurisdiction of the English courts. DPA cl. 13.1–13.2 vs MSA cl. 15.1–15.2

'Confidential Information' defined inconsistently: MSA requires written marking at disclosure; DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether or not marked. MSA cl. 11.1 vs DPA cl. 1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination although Provider must hold records and data (including confidential and personal data) for 7 years, leaving retained data unprotected. MSA cl. 11.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Subcontracting conflict: the MSA permits subcontracting of any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. MSA cl. 9.3 vs DPA cl. 5.1

Data location conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin as approved locations, yet the delivery team (which will access Customer data) operates from Bengaluru, India. DPA cl. 4.1, 4.3, Annex 2 vs SOW 1 cl. 3.4

The InfoSec Policy allows Customer data to be stored and processed in any Provider region as determined unilaterally by Provider's CISO, with notice only within 30 days after a new region enters service — directly contrary to the DPA's UK/EEA restriction and requirement of prior written authorisation. Phase durations total 36 months from 1 March 2027 (ending February 2030), which extends beyond both the 24-month MSA initial term (ending March 2029) and the 12-month Order Form term, so Phases 3 and 4 fall outside the contract term. SOW 1 cl. 4.1–4.4 vs MSA cl. 3.1 and Order Form cl. 1.2

'Fee' is defined by reference to MSA clause 4 (£12,400), yet the SLA and SOW compute service credits on 'the monthly Fee' where the SOW sets £12,800 — the credit base is ambiguous. MSA cl. 1.4 vs SOW cl. 5.1, 7.4 and SLA cl. 4.2

Provider is given a unilateral right to determine equivalent security controls and add regions, and to classify data, with no Customer approval, contradicting the requirement that Provider act only on Customer's documented instructions as processor. InfoSec cl. 1.4, 2.1 vs DPA cl. 2.2
unmatched: The Deliverable warranty is measured against 'applicable acceptance criteria' that are never set out anywhere in the document set, making the warranty unenforceable/indeterminate. MSA cl. 8.2 (with SOW 1 s. 6)

Deliverables are defined in the MSA as items identified in a Statement of Work, but the SOW leaves them to a phase plan unilaterally maintained by Provider's delivery lead — the scope of the Deliverables is therefore undefined and controlled by one party. MSA cl. 1.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 6.1

Internal contradiction: Provider must make records available to Customer on reasonable request 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 removes any right of inspection. MSA cl. 12.2 with cl. 10.2

Service report and change log retention limited to the duration of the Agreement conflicts with the 7-year post-termination retention obligation. SLA cl. 6.3 and Change Control cl. 9.3 vs MSA cl. 12.4

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, conflicting with the SOW's separate credit entitlement and with the MSA's general liability regime; combined with the differing caps, the remedy is indeterminate. SLA cl. 4.3 vs SOW 1 cl. 7.4 and MSA cl. 13.1

Inconsistent incident reporting deadlines for the same event: root cause analysis within 5 Business Days of Resolution versus written incident report within 10 Business Days of closing the incident, with no reconciliation. SLA cl. 8.1 vs InfoSec cl. 6.1–6.2

Response and Resolution times are measured from the moment Provider itself acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, making the 15-minute 'response' target circular and allowing Provider to control the clock start. SLA cl. 5.4

Transition assistance is chargeable and conditional on Customer approving an estimate before assistance begins, which can defeat the mandatory exit assistance obligation and conflicts with the SOW statement that the Fee covers all personnel; it also conflicts with cl. 2.2 requiring the Services to continue on the terms then in force. Exit Plan cl. 2.2, 3.1–3.4 vs SOW 1 cl. 5.2
The SOW prohibits substitution of 'named key personnel' but no key personnel are named in any document, so the obligation has no content. SOW 1 cl. 3.5

The DPA states Annex 1 sets out the processing details 'in full', but Annex 1 omits the nature of the processing operations and the retention period, and describes 'hosting Services' not covered by the SOW's scope description. DPA cl. 3.4 and Annex 1

Invoices without a valid purchase order number 'may be returned unpaid', which conflicts with the unqualified obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the stated payment period. Order Form cl. 5.3 vs MSA cl. 4.3

Document set is internally mislabelled: the cover labels state 'DOCUMENT 1 of 4' through 'DOCUMENT 4 of 4', but nine documents are included (Documents 5–9 are unnumbered as to the total), so the contract set's own description of its constituent documents is wrong. Headers of all documents (01–09)

Insurance conflict: professional indemnity cover of not less than £5,000,000 under the MSA versus not less than £2,000,000 under the SOW for the same services. MSA cl. 16.1; SOW cl. 9.4

Irreconcilable data retention/deletion obligations: the MSA requires all records, data and materials to be retained for 7 years after termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention for 90 days and then deletion. All three cannot be complied with. MSA cl. 12.4; DPA cl. 8.2; Exit Plan cl. 2.3, 5.2

Log retention conflict: security logs must be retained for 18 months 'and then deleted', which conflicts with the MSA's 7-year retention of all records evidencing performance (access logs being such records). InfoSec cl. 5.2; MSA cl. 12.4

Retention conflict: service reports and the change log are to be retained only 'for the duration of the Agreement', contradicting the MSA's 7-year post-termination retention requirement (and the Exit Plan's requirement to hand over the change log on exit). SLA cl. 6.3; Change Control cl. 9.3; MSA cl. 12.4; Exit Plan cl. 4.1(e)

'Confidential Information' conflict: the MSA limits it to information marked confidential at the time of disclosure, while the DPA declares all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked. Under the MSA precedence clause the narrower definition would defeat the DPA protection. MSA cl. 11.1; DPA cl. 1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination although data and records (including personal data) may lawfully be held for up to 7 years, leaving retained material unprotected. MSA cl. 11.3 with cl. 12.4

Encryption gap/conflict: the Information Security Policy mandates encryption at rest only for 'Restricted Data', so transaction records and loyalty identifiers (Internal Data) would not be encrypted, contradicting the DPA requirement for encryption at rest of all Customer Personal Data. InfoSec cl. 1.2–1.3, 3.1; DPA cl. 7.2

Recovery objective conflicts with the incident target: a Continuity Event renders the platform wholly unavailable and is therefore a Priority 1 Incident requiring Resolution within 4 hours, yet the BCDR RTO is 8 hours from Invocation. BCDR cl. 2.1; SLA cl. 1.3, 5.1

BCDR permits up to 12 hours of planned unavailability on return to the primary environment, which is incompatible with a 99.9% monthly availability target (about 43 minutes of downtime per month) and with the promise of 24x7 Priority 1 support; the blanket suspension of all SLA obligations during a Continuity Event also overrides the SLA without any corresponding carve-out in the SLA. BCDR cl. 5.1–5.3; SLA cl. 2.1, 3.1

Circular measurement of response times: response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute 'response' target measures nothing and Provider controls the start of the clock. SLA cl. 5.4 with cl. 5.1–5.3

'Sole financial remedy' clause conflicts with the rest of the set: service credits are stated to be Customer's only financial remedy for availability failure, which cannot stand with the SOW credit regime, the MSA general liability regime, or the DPA's disapplication of all limitations. SLA cl. 4.3; SOW cl. 7.4; MSA cl. 13.1; DPA cl. 11.1

Automatic application of service credits to invoices sits awkwardly with the MSA's prohibition on set-off, counterclaim, deduction or withholding without Provider's written agreement; no carve-out for credits is provided. SLA cl. 4.1; MSA cl. 4.5

'Deliverable' cannot be identified: the MSA defines a Deliverable as an item identified as such in a Statement of Work, but the SOW defers identification to a phase plan maintained unilaterally by Provider's delivery lead. Acceptance, IP assignment and warranty obligations therefore have no fixed object. MSA cl. 1.3; SOW cl. 6.1
The SOW prohibits substitution of 'named key personnel' but no key personnel are named anywhere in the contract set. SOW cl. 3.5

Deemed approval of Change Requests (10 Business Days) can expire while the escalation process (5 Business Days per level, three levels) is still running, and the Procedure expressly states escalation does not suspend the timetable — so a disputed change can be deemed approved mid-dispute. Change Control cl. 4.2, 8.1–8.3

Change-related charges are declared exempt from the notice requirements for charge increases, circumventing the MSA restriction that the Fee may be increased only once in any 12 months, on 60 days' notice and capped at CPI. Change Control cl. 5.3; MSA cl. 4.4

Provider's Delivery Lead may unilaterally approve changes up to £35,000 with no aggregate limit or frequency cap, permitting unlimited cumulative change without Customer approval and contradicting the requirement for bilateral written agreement. Change Control cl. 4.3; MSA cl. 2.4

Transition period start is undefined for expiry: it 'begins on the date notice of termination is given', yet the Plan applies however the Agreement ends, including natural expiry (no notice) and immediate termination for breach (no notice period). Exit Plan cl. 1.2, 2.1; MSA cl. 3.4

Provider must continue providing the Services for six months after the effective date of termination, but the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination and the Exit Plan itself allows only 90 days' retention — the Services cannot be delivered without the data. Exit Plan cl. 2.2–2.3; DPA cl. 8.2
Data return format conflict: the Exit Plan requires return 'in the format used by Provider's systems' while the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. Exit Plan cl. 4.1(a); DPA cl. 8.1

Customer approval of Provider's effort estimate is a precondition to transition assistance beginning, which can nullify Provider's unconditional obligation to provide transition assistance and stalls the Annex 1 milestones. Exit Plan cl. 3.1, 3.4, Annex 1

The Information Security Policy and the Change Control Procedure rely on a 'quarterly security review' and a 'monthly service review' that are only partly established elsewhere; the quarterly security review is not constituted in any governance clause (the SOW provides only a monthly service review and a quarterly steering committee). InfoSec cl. 6.3; SOW cl. 8.1–8.2

Internal inconsistency in remediation timescales: critical penetration test findings must be fixed within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no reconciliation of which applies to a critical patchable finding. InfoSec cl. 7.4, 9.1

Precedence ranking relegates the Data Processing Addendum to the lowest tier, so the MSA's denial of audit rights and its liability cap would override the DPA's audit, subprocessor-consent and unlimited-liability provisions, defeating the DPA's stated purpose. Order Form cl. 2.1(d); DPA cl. 11.1, 12.1

Order Form is signed and dated 12 March 2027 and purports to be issued under an MSA whose Effective Date is 1 April 2027; the document set contains no execution/counterpart provision reconciling the sequence. Order Form cl. 7.3; MSA Effective Date

Scope mismatch: the Order Form covers 'ongoing platform operation' as described in Statement of Work 1, but the SOW describes only a fixed-term replatforming programme with no ongoing operations service, and the fee is a single programme fee. Order Form cl. 1.1; SOW cl. 2.1, 5.1

Invoices without a purchase order number 'may be returned unpaid', which conflicts with the unqualified obligation to pay each undisputed invoice within the stated payment period. Order Form cl. 5.3; MSA cl. 4.3

Renewal mechanics conflict: the MSA renews the Agreement for successive 12-month periods terminable only on 90 days' notice, while the Order Form renews for 12-month periods terminable on 30 days' notice of non-renewal, so the Order Form can expire while the MSA term continues (and vice versa). MSA cl. 3.2–3.3; Order Form cl. 6.1–6.2

The set is internally mislabelled: each of the first four documents is headed 'DOCUMENT n of 4' and the instructions describe four documents, but nine documents are included (Order Form, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure and Exit Plan are unnumbered additions), leaving the composition of the 'Agreement' uncertain. Document headers, 01_msa.md through 09_exit.md

Single point of failure with no deputy: only Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, and Customer has no right to require invocation, so recovery can stall indefinitely during a Continuity Event. BCDR cl. 4.1

A Security Incident is deemed a Priority 1 Incident even though Priority 1 is defined as total unavailability, producing a classification that does not match the response/resolution model (e.g. a data-disclosure incident with no outage). SLA cl. 1.3, 7.2
Non-solicitation is limited to 'during the programme' with no post-termination tail, and there is no reciprocal restraint, leaving the protection ineffective once the SOW ends. SOW cl. 9.1

The SOW assumption that no more than three legacy interfaces require bespoke adapters has no stated consequence or link to the Change Control Procedure if the assumption proves wrong. SOW cl. 10.3; Change Control cl. 1.1

Mutual indemnity for regulatory fines is likely unenforceable and conflicts with the DPA's own no-limitation clause and with the MSA cap, with no allocation mechanism where both parties contribute to a breach. DPA cl. 11.2 with cl. 11.1; MSA cl. 13.1

Change Control cl. 7.2 (referencing Exit Plan cl. 3.2)

findings: Circular order of precedence: MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SoW 1 (a Schedule) says the SoW prevails over the MSA, and the Order Form says it prevails over every other document. The three rules cannot be reconciled and no document resolves the loop. 01_msa.md cl.14.2; 02_sow.md cl.1.2; 05_order_form.md cl.2.1–2.2

Monthly Fee stated in two different amounts: £12,400 in the MSA and £12,800 in SoW 1 (the Order Form's £153,600 ACV corresponds to £12,800, not £12,400, i.e. it implicitly contradicts the MSA). 01_msa.md cl.4.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.5.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.1.4
Three incompatible payment terms for the same invoices: 30 days from receipt, 45 days from receipt, and 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md cl.4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.5.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Three incompatible contract durations for the same engagement: MSA initial term 24 months, SoW programme 36 months, Order Form initial term 12 months. A 36-month programme cannot be performed within a 24-month (or 12-month) term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Start dates conflict: the MSA is effective 1 April 2027 and the Order Form's Service Commencement Date is 1 April 2027, but the SoW programme is said to commence 1 March 2027 — one month before the agreement exists. 01_msa.md Effective Date vs 02_sow.md cl.2.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl.1.3
The Order Form is dated/signed 12 March 2027, after the SoW's stated programme commencement of 1 March 2027. 05_order_form.md cl.7.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.2

Termination/renewal notice periods conflict: MSA requires 90 days' notice for convenience (and makes renewal avoidable only via cl.3.3), the SoW allows 30 days' notice, and the Order Form requires only 30 days' notice of non-renewal. 01_msa.md cl.3.2–3.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.3 vs 05_order_form.md cl.6.1–6.2

Acceptance mechanism contradiction: MSA states no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer expressly confirms in writing, while the SoW deems Deliverables accepted by Customer silence after 5 Business Days. 01_msa.md cl.6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.3

Reference to a non-existent provision: MSA points to acceptance criteria in "Schedule 1, Section 12", but SoW 1 (Schedule 1) contains only sections 1–10 and states no acceptance criteria at all. 01_msa.md cl.6.2 (referring to 02_sow.md)

No acceptance criteria exist anywhere, yet the warranty in MSA cl.8.2 (conformity to "applicable acceptance criteria") and the Change Control Procedure's coverage of changes to acceptance criteria both depend on them. 01_msa.md cl.8.2; 08_change_control.md cl.1.1

Deliverables are defined only by a "phase plan maintained by the delivery lead", i.e. unilaterally by Provider, which conflicts with the MSA requirement that Deliverables be identified in a Statement of Work and that changes be agreed in writing. 02_sow.md cl.6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.3 and cl.2.4

Liability cap conflict: MSA caps each party's liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap prevails notwithstanding any Schedule, while the SoW imposes a £250,000 cap on Provider only; the two caps produce different figures and the MSA cap is mutual whereas the SoW cap is one-sided. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.2

The DPA disapplies all limitations and exclusions of liability for any breach of the Addendum or of Data Protection Law, which directly contradicts the MSA's statement that its cap applies notwithstanding any other provision of any Schedule or Addendum, and the MSA precedence clause. 03_dpa.md cl.11.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.3, 14.2
Insurance limits conflict: professional indemnity cover of not less than £5,000,000 in the MSA versus not less than £2,000,000 in the SoW. 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4
Availability target stated twice at different levels: 99.5% per month in the SoW and 99.9% per month in the SLA Schedule. 02_sow.md cl.7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1
Service credit caps conflict: up to 25% of the monthly Fee in the SoW versus a maximum of 10% of the monthly Fee in the SLA Schedule. 02_sow.md cl.7.4 vs 04_sla.md cl.4.2

Service level start date conflict: the SoW applies service levels only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme), whereas the Order Form states service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md cl.7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.3

Support coverage conflict: the SLA provides Priority 2 and 3 support only 08:00–18:00 on Business Days, while the Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md cl.2.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.1

"Business Day" is defined two incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA). The US-holiday definition is also incongruent with an England and Wales governed contract, and it is unclear which definition applies in the InfoSec, BCDR, Change Control and Exit schedules that use the term. 01_msa.md cl.1.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.1.1

"Security Incident" is defined twice and inconsistently: the DPA's broad definition (any unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction) versus the SLA's narrow definition (confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of data); the InfoSec Policy uses a third formulation ("confirmed security incident"). 03_dpa.md cl.1.6 vs 04_sla.md cl.7.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.6.1

Three irreconcilable security incident notification deadlines for the same event: 24 hours (DPA), 48 hours (InfoSec Policy) and 72 hours (SLA). 03_dpa.md cl.6.1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.6.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.7.3

Internal inconsistency: a Security Incident is deemed a Priority 1 Incident with a 4-hour Resolution target, yet notification of it to Customer is permitted up to 72 hours after confirmation. 04_sla.md cl.7.2 vs cl.7.3

Cross-reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to "Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum" for security escalation contacts; the DPA has only Annexes 1 and 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4 (referring to 03_dpa.md)
Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan refers to "the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14"; the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3 (referring to 03_dpa.md)

Cross-reference to a non-existent clause and body: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to "the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17"; the MSA ends at clause 16 and creates no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1 (referring to 01_msa.md)

Misdirected cross-reference: impact-assessment charges for rejected changes are said to be "at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan", but that Plan sets only a transition-assistance day rate (£1,250) and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2 (referring to 09_exit.md cl.3.2)

Audit rights contradiction: the MSA states Customer has no right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems beyond receipt of a SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems, and the InfoSec Policy contemplates penetration test participation and security reviews. 01_msa.md cl.10.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1–9.2; 06_infosec.md cl.7.3, 6.3

Self-defeating cross-reference: Provider must make records available to Customer "in accordance with clause 10.2", but clause 10.2 removes any inspection right, so the records obligation has no mechanism. 01_msa.md cl.12.2 with cl.10.2

Subcontracting contradiction: the MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md cl.9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.5.1

Data location contradiction: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and to the locations in Annex 2 (London and Dublin only), but the SoW places the delivery team (with system access) in Bengaluru, India, and the InfoSec Policy lets Provider's CISO unilaterally choose any Provider region. 03_dpa.md cl.4.1–4.3 & Annex 2 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.4 vs 06_infosec.md cl.2.1

The BCDR recovery environment is in Frankfurt, Germany, which is not among the approved processing locations listed in DPA Annex 2 (London, Dublin) and has not been authorised under DPA cl.4.2. 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.3 & Annex 2

The InfoSec Policy allows new processing regions to be notified up to 30 days after they enter service, which is incompatible with the DPA's requirement of prior written authorisation before any transfer. 06_infosec.md cl.2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.2

Data retention/deletion obligations cannot all be satisfied: the MSA requires all records, data and materials to be retained for 7 years after termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days after termination. 01_msa.md cl.12.4 vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.2.3

Log/report retention conflicts with the MSA's 7-year record retention: security logs must be retained 18 months "and then deleted", service reports only "for the duration of the Agreement", and the change log only "for the duration of the Agreement". 06_infosec.md cl.5.2; 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4

Confidentiality definition conflict: the MSA protects only information marked confidential at the time of disclosure, whereas the DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; under the MSA precedence clause the narrower definition would prevail and strip protection from unmarked personal data. 01_msa.md cl.11.1 & 14.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination, which is inconsistent with the 7-year record retention obligation and with indefinite data protection duties over retained personal data. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md

Governing law conflict: the MSA is governed by the laws of England and Wales with exclusive English jurisdiction, but the DPA states it is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md cl.15.1–15.2 vs 03_dpa.md cl.13.2

Internal contradiction within the DPA governing law clause: cl.13.1 adopts the law applicable to the Agreement while cl.13.2 imposes Irish law, so the clause contradicts itself. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1 vs 13.2

The DPA clause headed "PRECEDENCE" states only that the Addendum forms part of the Agreement; it contains no precedence rule, leaving the DPA's overriding provisions (e.g. cl.11.1, 1.4) unsupported against the MSA precedence clause. 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

Change approval contradiction: the MSA requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 01_msa.md cl.2.4 vs 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1

Internal inconsistency in change approval: cl.4.1 requires submission to a Change Control Board, yet cl.4.2 allows approval by Customer silence and cl.4.3 lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve alone; there is also no aggregate limit on repeated £35,000 approvals. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1–4.3

Change-related charges are expressly exempted from the notice requirements applying to ordinary increases, allowing the MSA's 60-day notice and CPI cap on fee increases to be circumvented. 08_change_control.md cl.5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.4

Mismatched escalation paths for the same programme: delivery lead → account director → executive sponsor (SoW) versus Delivery Lead → Programme Director → Chief Information Officer (Change Control); neither Programme Director nor CIO is a role defined or named anywhere. 02_sow.md cl.8.3 vs 08_change_control.md cl.8.1

Wrong internal cross-reference: escalation is said not to suspend "the timetable in clause 3" (impact assessment), but escalation under clause 8 arises out of approval/rejection under clauses 4 and 7, so the reference is inapt. 08_change_control.md cl.8.3

Response and Resolution times are measured from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, making the response target circular (Provider must respond within 15 minutes of its own acknowledgement) and leaving the time between Customer report and acknowledgement unmeasured. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 with cl.5.1–5.3

Service credits are stated as an entitlement with a cap but no calculation method or tiering is given in either document, and the "monthly Fee" to which the percentage applies is itself disputed (£12,400 vs £12,800). 04_sla.md cl.4.1–4.2; 02_sow.md cl.7.4

"Sole financial remedy" clause conflicts with the SoW credit entitlement and with the general liability regime and DPA carve-out, and it is unclear whether it survives the MSA precedence clause. 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.13; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1

Recovery objectives are mathematically incompatible with the availability commitment: a single 8-hour RTO event (plus up to 12 further hours of planned unavailability on return) far exceeds the ~43 minutes of monthly downtime permitted by 99.9% availability. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1

The BCDR Plan suspends all Service Level Schedule obligations for the (open-ended) duration of a Continuity Event and excludes return-to-primary downtime from availability, but the SLA's exclusions list contains no such exclusion and permits exclusion only of agreed maintenance windows notified 5 Business Days in advance. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1–5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.3, 3.4, 9.1–9.3

Encryption obligations conflict: the DPA requires encryption of Customer Personal Data at rest, but the InfoSec Policy requires encryption at rest only for "Restricted Data", leaving personal data classified as Internal Data unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.3.1, 1.3

Data categories are inconsistent: the DPA limits personal data to contact details, transaction records and loyalty identifiers, while the InfoSec Policy contemplates Provider holding employee compensation data and payment card data, which are outside the authorised processing scope and Annex 1. 03_dpa.md cl.3.3 & Annex 1 vs 06_infosec.md cl.1.2

The InfoSec Policy (a Schedule) may be reviewed and materially changed by Provider with only notice to Customer, permitting unilateral amendment of a contract document contrary to the requirement for bilateral written change. 06_infosec.md cl.10.1–10.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4, 1.6

Remediation timescales inconsistent: critical penetration test findings must be remediated within 30 days while critical security patches must be applied within 14 days, with no reconciliation for critical findings that are patch-related. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

Data return format conflict: the DPA requires return in a structured, commonly used format, while the Exit Plan requires return "in the format used by Provider's systems" (potentially proprietary). 03_dpa.md cl.8.1 vs 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a)

The Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing the Services until 6 months after the effective date of termination, which cannot be reconciled with immediate termination for material breach or with the fixed term/notice provisions, and no charging basis for that post-termination period is stated. 09_exit.md cl.2.1–2.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.1, 3.4

Transition assistance is conditional on Customer approving Provider's estimate before assistance begins, which conflicts with the unconditional obligation to provide exit assistance however the Agreement ends and lets Provider withhold assistance pending commercial agreement. 09_exit.md cl.3.4 vs cl.1.2, 3.1

The Exit Plan is triggered only by expiry or termination of the Agreement, with no provision for termination of the Statement of Work alone, which the SoW expressly permits without terminating the MSA. 09_exit.md cl.1.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.2.3–2.4

The Order Form is not part of the "Agreement" as defined (MSA + Schedules + Addenda executed under it); it is neither a Schedule nor an Addendum, yet it purports to sit at the top of the precedence order, and its precedence list omits its own document class from the MSA's definitional scheme. 05_order_form.md cl.2.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6

The Order Form permits invoices lacking a purchase order number to be returned unpaid, which conflicts with the MSA's obligation to pay without set-off, deduction or withholding except as required by law or agreed by Provider. 05_order_form.md cl.5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.5

The Order Form contracts for "ongoing platform operation" but the SoW describes only a four-phase replatforming programme ending in stabilisation and handover; no ongoing operation service, scope or charge is defined. 05_order_form.md cl.1.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.4.1–4.4

The SoW prohibits substitution of "named key personnel", but no key personnel are named in any document (the Order Form lists only role titles), so the restriction has no content. 02_sow.md cl.3.5; 05_order_form.md cl.4.4

Ambiguous/reversed indemnity: "Each party shall indemnify the other against fines imposed on it as a result of the other's breach" is internally incoherent about whose breach and whose fine is covered, and purports to indemnify regulatory fines that may be uninsurable/unenforceable. 03_dpa.md cl.11.2

Only Provider's Head of Operations may declare an Invocation, with no deputy or alternate and no right for Customer to require invocation, creating a single point of failure in the recovery process; the definition of Continuity Event is also circular/subjective ("cannot be resolved within normal support processes"). 07_bcdr.md cl.4.1, 1.2

Inconsistent time units within and between schedules (calendar months versus Business Days) for linked obligations, e.g. remediation plan "within one (1) month" against test reports in Business Days, and Exit Annex 1 milestones in Business Days against a transition period expressed in months. 07_bcdr.md cl.6.3–6.4; 09_exit.md Annex 1 vs cl.2.1

Priority 2 Resolution is targeted at one Business Day while Priority 2 support is only available 08:00–18:00 on Business Days, so out-of-hours degradation has no coverage and the target cannot be measured consistently; the Order Form's 24x7 promise compounds the ambiguity. 04_sla.md cl.2.2, 5.2 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.1

Rejected-Deliverable remedies are inconsistent: the MSA requires correction and resubmission at no charge with no deadline, while the SoW imposes a 10 Business Day resubmission deadline and is silent on cost. 01_msa.md cl.6.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.4

Document set labelling is wrong: each of the first four documents is headed "DOCUMENT n of 4" although the contract set comprises nine documents (Order Form and Schedules 3–6 are unnumbered in that series). 01_msa.md–04_sla.md headers vs 05_order_form.md–09_exit.md

The MSA lists no schedules and defines only "Schedule" and "Addendum" generically; there is no annexure/document list identifying Schedules 2–6 and the Order Form, so the composition of the Agreement is uncertain. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6, 2.1

The 90-day Deliverable warranty runs from acceptance, but acceptance can occur by deemed acceptance without any conformity assessment, and the criteria against which conformity is judged do not exist. 01_msa.md cl.8.2 with cl.6.1–6.2 and 02_sow.md cl.6.3

The Change Control Procedure states an approved change takes effect immediately while revised charges apply only from the next invoice issued, leaving unpaid work performed between approval and the next invoice unaddressed. 08_change_control.md cl.4.4 vs cl.5.1

The Exit Plan requires delivery of "the outstanding change log" but the Change Control Procedure requires the change log to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, so it may lawfully be destroyed at the moment it must be handed over. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(e) vs 08_change_control.md cl.9.3

Exclusion conflict: the BCDR Plan suspends SLA obligations and excludes Continuity Event downtime from the availability calculation, but the SLA excludes only agreed maintenance windows and its exclusions list does not mention Continuity Events. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1 & 5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.3 & 9

The 12 hours of planned unavailability for return to the primary environment cannot satisfy the SLA requirement of 5 Business Days' prior notice of a maintenance window. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.4

Service credits applied automatically to the next invoice amount to a deduction/set-off, conflicting with the MSA requirement to pay all amounts without set-off, counterclaim or deduction. 04_sla.md cl.4.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.5

Remedies conflict: SLA makes service credits Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, while the SOW grants a separate service credit entitlement and neither addresses the MSA's general remedies/termination for material breach. 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.3.4

Circular/unenforceable measurement: response and Resolution times run from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, so the 15-minute 'response' target measures nothing and Provider controls the clock start; no target for acknowledgement is set. 04_sla.md cl.5.4 & 5.1

Internal contradiction in the Exit Plan: Provider must retain Customer data for only 90 days after termination and then delete it, yet must deliver all Customer data at the end of a transition period ending six months after termination. 09_exit.md cl.2.3, 4.1(a), 5.2
Data return format conflict: Exit Plan requires return 'in the format used by Provider's systems', while the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a) vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Exit assistance obligation is blocked by a condition precedent: Provider must give reasonable transition assistance and meet a T+15 Business Day milestone, yet assistance cannot begin until Customer approves an estimate that Provider has up to 15 Business Days to produce. 09_exit.md cl.3.1, 3.3, 3.4 & Annex 1 milestone 1

Annex 1 milestones run from the effective date of termination (T), whereas the transition period is defined as beginning on the date notice is given — two different clocks for the same programme, and for immediate termination for breach the notice and termination dates coincide, compressing the timetable. 09_exit.md cl.2.1 & Annex 1
