findings: Document set is internally mislabelled: documents 1–4 are headed "DOCUMENT n of 4" but the contract set actually contains nine documents (Order Form, InfoSec Policy, BCDR Plan, Change Control Procedure and Exit Plan are additional), so the stated document count and numbering are wrong and it is unclear whether documents 5–9 form part of the Agreement. Headers of 01_msa.md, 02_sow.md, 03_dpa.md, 04_sla.md vs Documents 5–9

Circular / irreconcilable order of precedence: MSA cl.14.2 says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum; SOW cl.1.2 says the SOW (which is Schedule 1) prevails over the MSA; Order Form cl.2.1–2.2 says the Order Form prevails over everything including the MSA. No document can be ranked consistently. 01_msa.md cl.14.2; 02_sow.md cl.1.2; 05_order_form.md cl.2.1–2.2

The Order Form claims top precedence but is not part of the "Agreement" as defined: MSA cl.1.1 defines the Agreement as the MSA plus each Schedule and Addendum only, and cl.1.6 requires a Schedule to be expressly stated to be a Schedule. An Order Form is neither, so its precedence clause has no contractual hook. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6 vs 05_order_form.md cl.2.1

Monthly Fee stated in three inconsistent ways: MSA £12,400/month; SOW £12,800/month; Order Form Annual Contract Value £153,600 (= £12,800 x 12, i.e. consistent with the SOW but not the MSA). 01_msa.md cl.4.1; 02_sow.md cl.5.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.4

Three conflicting payment terms: 30 days from receipt of invoice (MSA), 45 days from receipt (SOW), 60 days from invoice date (Order Form). The trigger event also differs (receipt vs invoice date). 01_msa.md cl.4.3; 02_sow.md cl.5.3; 05_order_form.md cl.1.6

Three conflicting term lengths: MSA initial term 24 months; SOW programme duration 36 months; Order Form Initial Term 12 months. The 36-month programme cannot be completed within either the 24-month or the 12-month term. 01_msa.md cl.3.1; 02_sow.md cl.2.1; 05_order_form.md cl.1.2

Start-date conflict: the SOW programme commences 1 March 2027, one month before the MSA Effective Date (1 April 2027) and before the Order Form was signed (12 March 2027) and before the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). Services are scheduled to start before the contract exists. 02_sow.md cl.2.2 vs 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md cl.1.3, 7.3

Conflicting termination-for-convenience notice periods: 90 days under the MSA, 30 days for the SOW, and 30 days' non-renewal notice under the Order Form (which also conflicts with MSA cl.3.2/3.3 requiring 90 days' notice to prevent auto-renewal). 01_msa.md cl.3.3, 3.2; 02_sow.md cl.2.3; 05_order_form.md cl.6.2

"Business Day" is defined two incompatible ways: Monday–Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays (MSA) versus Monday–Saturday excluding US federal holidays (SLA). Every SLA response/resolution deadline and every other document's Business Day deadline is therefore ambiguous. 01_msa.md cl.1.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.1.1
Conflicting availability service levels for the same platform: 99.5% per month (SOW) versus 99.9% per month (SLA). 02_sow.md cl.7.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1

Conflicting service credit caps: up to 25% of the monthly Fee (SOW) versus not exceeding 10% of the monthly Fee (SLA). The "monthly Fee" is itself ambiguous (£12,400 or £12,800). 02_sow.md cl.7.4 vs 04_sla.md cl.4.2

Conflicting start of service level regime: SOW says service levels apply only from the start of Phase 3 (month 19 of the programme); Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date (1 April 2027). 02_sow.md cl.7.1 vs 05_order_form.md cl.3.3

Conflicting support coverage: Order Form promises 24x7 support for all priority levels, while the SLA limits Priority 2 and 3 support to 08:00–18:00 on Business Days. 05_order_form.md cl.3.1 vs 04_sla.md cl.2.2

"Security Incident" defined two incompatible ways: DPA covers any unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction (no confirmation required); SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption of data. The narrower SLA definition would exclude most DPA-notifiable events. 03_dpa.md cl.1.6 vs 04_sla.md cl.7.1

Three conflicting security incident notification deadlines: within 24 hours of awareness (DPA), within 72 hours of confirmation (SLA), within 48 hours of confirmation (InfoSec Policy). The trigger (awareness vs confirmation) also differs. 03_dpa.md cl.6.1; 04_sla.md cl.7.3; 06_infosec.md cl.6.1

Cross-reference to a non-existent annex: the SLA points to "Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum" for security escalation contacts, but the DPA contains only Annex 1 and Annex 2. 04_sla.md cl.7.4 vs 03_dpa.md Annexes
Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: the Exit Plan refers to "the Data Processing Addendum, clause 14", but the DPA ends at clause 13. 09_exit.md cl.5.3 vs 03_dpa.md

Cross-reference to a non-existent clause: the Change Control Procedure submits Change Requests to "the Change Control Board described in the Master Services Agreement, clause 17", but the MSA ends at clause 16 and contains no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md cl.4.1 vs 01_msa.md

Cross-reference to a non-existent section: MSA requires Deliverables to be assessed against acceptance criteria "set out in Schedule 1, Section 12", but the SOW (Schedule 1) has only 10 sections and contains no acceptance criteria at all. 01_msa.md cl.6.2 vs 02_sow.md

Acceptance mechanism directly contradictory: MSA says no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer confirms acceptance expressly in writing; SOW deems a Deliverable accepted if Customer is silent for 5 Business Days. 01_msa.md cl.6.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.6.3

Warranty is unworkable because it is tied to acceptance criteria that no document contains: MSA warrants conformity with "the applicable acceptance criteria", and Deliverables themselves are defined only by a phase plan unilaterally maintained by Provider's delivery lead. 01_msa.md cl.8.2, 6.2; 02_sow.md cl.6.1

Audit rights contradictory: MSA states that after delivery of the SOC 2 report Customer has "no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems", while the DPA grants an annual on-site audit including inspection of premises and systems (and InfoSec/BCDR presuppose reviews and test participation). 01_msa.md cl.10.2 (and cl.12.2) vs 03_dpa.md cl.9.1–9.2

Subcontracting contradictory: MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA prohibits engaging any Subprocessor without Customer's prior written consent to that specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md cl.9.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.5.1

Data location obligations cannot all be satisfied: DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA with prior authorisation for transfers; the SOW places the delivery team (which requires system access) in Bengaluru, India; the InfoSec Policy allows storage/processing in any Provider region as unilaterally determined by Provider's CISO with only 30 days' after-the-fact notice. 03_dpa.md cl.4.1–4.2 vs 02_sow.md cl.3.4 and 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 2.3

Approved processing locations do not include the disaster recovery site actually used: DPA Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin, while the BCDR Plan operates the secondary recovery environment in Frankfurt, Germany, to which data is replicated. 03_dpa.md Annex 2 vs 07_bcdr.md cl.3.1, 3.3

Governing law conflict and internal contradiction: MSA is governed by England and Wales with exclusive English jurisdiction; DPA cl.13.1 says it follows the Agreement's law "save as provided in clause 13.2", and cl.13.2 then selects the laws of the Republic of Ireland — contradicting both cl.13.1 and the MSA. 03_dpa.md cl.13.1–13.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.15.1–15.2

Data retention/deletion obligations are mutually impossible: MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years after termination; DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination; Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days after termination; InfoSec requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months. 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2; 09_exit.md cl.2.3, 5.2; 06_infosec.md cl.5.2

Record retention conflicts within the schedules: SLA requires service reports and Change Control requires the change log to be retained only "for the duration of the Agreement", contradicting the MSA's 7-year post-termination retention obligation (and the Exit Plan's requirement to hand the change log over at exit). 04_sla.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.12.4; 09_exit.md cl.4.1(e)
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance limits for the same Provider: £5,000,000 (MSA) versus £2,000,000 (SOW). 01_msa.md cl.16.1 vs 02_sow.md cl.9.4

Conflicting liability caps: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees (approx. £148,800–£153,600) and states in cl.13.3 that this applies notwithstanding any Schedule; the SOW sets a £250,000 cap; the DPA disapplies all limitations for breach of the Addendum or Data Protection Law. The three cannot coexist. 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md cl.9.2; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1

"Sole remedy" clause conflicts with other remedies: SLA states service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, which conflicts with the SOW's separate credit regime, the MSA's general liability regime, and the DPA's disapplication of limitations. 04_sla.md cl.4.3 vs 02_sow.md cl.7.4; 01_msa.md cl.13.1; 03_dpa.md cl.11.1

Automatic service credit set-off conflicts with the no-deduction clause: SLA requires Provider to apply credits automatically to the next invoice, whereas the MSA requires payment in full without set-off, deduction or withholding except as agreed by Provider in writing. 04_sla.md cl.4.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.5

"Confidential Information" defined inconsistently: MSA limits it to information marked confidential in writing at the time of disclosure; DPA deems all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked. Under MSA cl.14.2 the narrower definition would prevail, defeating the DPA provision. 01_msa.md cl.11.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.1.4

Confidentiality obligations expire 3 years after termination, yet records and personal data are to be held for up to 7 years, leaving retained data unprotected; there is also no carve-out for personal data, which must be protected indefinitely under Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md cl.11.3 vs cl.12.4; 03_dpa.md

Change control contradicts the MSA change requirement: MSA cl.2.4 requires every change to the Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, while the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval on Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes with no prior approval. 08_change_control.md cl.4.2, 4.3, 6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.2.4

Change-charge provision circumvents the price-increase protections: MSA cl.4.4 limits Fee increases to once per 12 months, on 60 days' notice, capped at CPI, but the Change Control Procedure states change-related charges are not subject to those notice requirements and apply from the next invoice. 08_change_control.md cl.5.1, 5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.4

Cross-reference points to a rate that does not exist: Change Control charges impact-assessment work "at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan", but the Exit Plan only sets a transition assistance rate (£1,250 per person per day) and no impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md cl.7.2 vs 09_exit.md cl.3.2

Internal mis-reference in escalation clause: cl.8.3 says escalation does not suspend "the timetable in clause 3" (Provider's own impact assessment timetable), when the relevant timetable for a disagreement about approval is in clause 4; the deemed-approval clock in cl.4.2 is also not addressed, so a Customer escalation can result in deemed approval. 08_change_control.md cl.8.3 (and cl.4.2)

Recovery objectives are incompatible with the availability service level: an 8-hour RTO plus up to 12 hours' planned unavailability on failback (up to 20 hours) far exceeds the ~43 minutes of monthly downtime permitted by 99.9% availability, and also exceeds the 4-hour Priority 1 Resolution target. 07_bcdr.md cl.2.1, 5.2 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.1, 5.1

Exclusion/suspension conflict: the BCDR Plan excludes Continuity Event downtime from the availability calculation and suspends SLA obligations, but the SLA's calculation and exclusions list (cl.3.2–3.3, cl.9) permit exclusion only of agreed maintenance windows, Customer-caused and third-party outages. Under MSA precedence the SLA text would override the BCDR carve-out. 07_bcdr.md cl.5.1–5.3 vs 04_sla.md cl.3.2–3.3, cl.9

Response and Resolution times are measured from the moment Provider acknowledges the Incident in its own tool, which makes the response target self-referential (always met) and lets Provider control the start of the clock rather than measuring from Customer report or Incident detection. 04_sla.md cl.5.4

Encryption obligations conflict: DPA requires encryption at rest for all Customer Personal Data, while the InfoSec Policy requires encryption at rest only for "Restricted Data", leaving personal data classified as "Internal Data" unencrypted. 03_dpa.md cl.7.2 vs 06_infosec.md cl.3.1, 1.2–1.3

Exit data format conflicts with DPA return format: Exit Plan requires return of Customer data "in the format used by Provider's systems" whereas the DPA requires a structured, commonly used format. 09_exit.md cl.4.1(a), 5.1 vs 03_dpa.md cl.8.1

Exit transition period is unworkable against the termination and deletion regimes: services must continue for 6 months after the effective date of termination (including after immediate termination for material breach), yet the MSA gives no post-termination service obligation or pricing, and Customer data is deleted at 90 days (Exit cl.2.3) or 30 days (DPA cl.8.2) — before handover certification at the end of the 6-month period. 09_exit.md cl.2.1–2.3, 4.1, Annex 1 milestone 5 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.4; 03_dpa.md cl.8.2

Transition period has no start date on expiry: it "begins on the date notice of termination is given", but the Plan expressly applies however the Agreement ends, including expiry without notice. 09_exit.md cl.2.1 vs cl.1.2

Exit assistance obligation is self-defeating: Provider need not begin assistance until Customer approves an effort estimate (which Provider has 15 Business Days to produce), yet Annex 1 milestone 1 falls due at T+15 Business Days and milestone 2 at T+30 Business Days. 09_exit.md cl.3.3–3.4 vs Annex 1 milestones 1–2
Clause headed "PRECEDENCE" contains no precedence rule at all, leaving the DPA's rank against the MSA, SOW and Order Form unresolved (particularly on liability and governing law). 03_dpa.md cl.12.1

Schedules 2–6 are not validly incorporated: MSA cl.1.6 requires a Schedule to be executed by both parties and expressly stated to be a Schedule, but only the Order Form bears signature provisions and the MSA never refers to Schedules 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6. 01_msa.md cl.1.1, 1.6 vs 04_sla.md, 06_infosec.md, 07_bcdr.md, 08_change_control.md, 09_exit.md headers

New processing regions may be added by Provider's CISO with notice only 30 days after they enter service, which is impossible to reconcile with the DPA requirement for prior written authorisation and an appropriate transfer mechanism before any transfer. 06_infosec.md cl.2.1, 2.3 vs 03_dpa.md cl.4.2

Remediation timescales inconsistent for the same class of risk: critical penetration-test findings within 30 days but critical security patches within 14 days, with no rule for which applies to a critical finding remediable by patching. 06_infosec.md cl.7.4 vs cl.9.1

Governance forums are duplicated and inconsistent across schedules: monthly service review and quarterly steering committee (SOW), quarterly security review (InfoSec), monthly review of the change log (Change Control) and monthly review of the corrective action register (SLA), with no single governance structure or reconciliation. 02_sow.md cl.8.1–8.2; 06_infosec.md cl.6.3; 08_change_control.md cl.9.2; 04_sla.md cl.8.3

Escalation ladders are inconsistent: SOW escalates delivery lead > account director > executive sponsor, while Change Control escalates Delivery Lead > Programme Director > Chief Information Officer; neither maps to the Order Form's named contacts (Head of Procurement, Director of Digital Platforms, Account Director). 02_sow.md cl.8.3; 08_change_control.md cl.8.1; 05_order_form.md cl.4

Purchase-order condition conflicts with the payment obligation: the Order Form allows invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, while the MSA obliges Customer to pay every undisputed invoice within 30 days, and no mechanism exists for the PO to be kept valid for the full term or increased for change charges. 05_order_form.md cl.5.1–5.3 vs 01_msa.md cl.4.3

Provider-controlled definition of scope undermines the Deliverable definition and IP assignment: Deliverables are those listed in a phase plan "maintained by the delivery lead" (Provider), whereas the MSA defines a Deliverable as an item identified in a Statement of Work and assigns IP only in Deliverables. 02_sow.md cl.6.1 vs 01_msa.md cl.1.3, 7.2

Key-personnel protection is unenforceable as drafted: the SOW prohibits substitution of "named key personnel" but no personnel are named anywhere in the SOW or Order Form (the Order Form identifies only roles). 02_sow.md cl.3.5; 05_order_form.md cl.4

Indemnity for regulatory fines is drafted mutually and without cap or conduct provisions, and conflicts with the MSA cap (which cl.13.3 says applies notwithstanding any Addendum); it may also be unenforceable to the extent fines are non-indemnifiable. 03_dpa.md cl.11.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.13.1, 13.3

Phase overlap rule conflicts with the fixed programme duration: phases total exactly 36 months and may overlap only by written agreement, so any single-phase slippage necessarily breaches the 36-month duration in cl.2.1 with no float or relief mechanism. 02_sow.md cl.2.1, 4.1–4.5

Non-renewal/termination mechanics of the Order Form and the SOW leave the MSA in place with no priced Services (SOW termination on 30 days' notice does not terminate the MSA, and the Order Form may lapse on 30 days' notice) while the MSA's monthly Fee obligation in cl.4.1 continues. 02_sow.md cl.2.4; 05_order_form.md cl.6.1–6.2 vs 01_msa.md cl.3.2, 4.1

Priority 2 Resolution target of one Business Day cannot be met consistently because Priority 2 support is only available 08:00–18:00 on Business Days, and the Business Day definition is itself disputed between documents. 04_sla.md cl.5.2 vs cl.2.2, cl.1.1

BCDR Plan is unilaterally controlled by Provider with no Customer remedy: only Provider's Head of Operations may invoke, Provider owns and amends the Plan, and there is no consequence for failing an annual test beyond producing a remediation plan; the Plan also excludes simultaneous loss of primary and recovery environments without any alternative arrangement. 07_bcdr.md cl.4.1, 6.4, 8.2, 9.1–9.3
